 4779: 
 4780: pub fn execute_ops_vm_lab_setup_live_lab(
 4781:     config: VmLabSetupLiveLabConfig,
 4782: ) -> Result<String, String> {
 4783:     ensure_local_regular_file_path(config.script_path.as_path(), "live-lab script")?;
 4784:     ensure_local_regular_file_path(config.ssh_identity_file.as_path(), "SSH identity file")?;
 4785:     ensure_optional_local_regular_file_path(
 4786:         config.known_hosts_path.as_deref(),
 4787:         "SSH known_hosts file",
 4788:     )?;
 4789:     if let Some(stage) = config.resume_from.as_deref()
 4790:         && !setup_stage_names().contains(&stage)
 4791:     {
 4792:         return Err(format!(
 4793:             "unsupported --resume-from stage for vm-lab-setup-live-lab: {stage}"
 4794:         ));
 4795:     }
 4796:     if let Some(stage) = config.rerun_stage.as_deref()
 4797:         && !setup_stage_names().contains(&stage)
 4798:     {
 4799:         return Err(format!(
 4800:             "unsupported --rerun-stage for vm-lab-setup-live-lab: {stage}"
 4801:         ));
 4802:     }
 4803:     if config.resume_from.is_some() && config.rerun_stage.is_some() {
 4804:         return Err(
 4805:             "vm-lab-setup-live-lab accepts either --resume-from or --rerun-stage, not both"
 4806:                 .to_string(),
 4807:         );
 4808:     }
 4809:     let report_dir = resolve_absolute_path(config.report_dir.as_path())?;
 4810:     let setup_reuse_requested = config.resume_from.is_some() || config.rerun_stage.is_some();
 4811:     if setup_reuse_requested {
 4812:         if !report_dir.exists() {
 4813:             return Err(format!(
 4814:                 "vm-lab-setup-live-lab resume/rerun requires an existing report dir: {}",
 4815:                 report_dir.display()
 4816:             ));
 4817:         }
 4818:         if !report_dir_contains_regular_entries(report_dir.as_path())? {
 4819:             return Err(format!(
 4820:                 "vm-lab-setup-live-lab resume/rerun requires an existing provenance-bound report dir with setup state: {}",
 4821:                 report_dir.display()
 4822:             ));
 4823:         }
 4824:     } else if config.orchestrated {
 4825:         // Called from vm-lab-orchestrate-live-lab, which has already claimed this report dir
 4826:         // and written pre-setup discovery metadata into the `orchestration/` subdirectory.
 4827:         // Exempt that directory from the freshness check; every other entry still blocks reuse.
 4828:         ensure_report_dir_fresh_except(
 4829:             report_dir.as_path(),
 4830:             "vm-lab-setup-live-lab",
 4831:             &["orchestration"],
 4832:         )?;
 4833:     } else {
 4834:         ensure_report_dir_fresh(report_dir.as_path(), "vm-lab-setup-live-lab")?;
 4835:     }
 4836:     fs::create_dir_all(report_dir.as_path()).map_err(|err| {
 4837:         format!(
 4838:             "create setup report directory failed ({}): {err}",
 4839:             report_dir.display()
 4840:         )
 4841:     })?;
 4842:     let (resolved_source_mode, resolved_repo_ref) = resolve_iteration_source_selection(
 4843:         config.source_mode.as_deref(),
 4844:         config.repo_ref.as_deref(),
 4845:         false,
 4846:         false,
 4847:         false,
 4848:     )?;
 4849:     let selection = if setup_reuse_requested {
 4850:         let selection = match config.profile_path.as_deref() {
 4851:             Some(profile_path) => {
 4852:                 execute_ops_vm_lab_validate_live_lab_profile(VmLabValidateLiveLabProfileConfig {
 4853:                     profile_path: profile_path.to_path_buf(),
 4854:                     expected_backend: None,
 4855:                     expected_source_mode: None,
 4856:                     require_five_node: false,
 4857:                 })?;
 4858:                 LiveLabSetupSelection {
 4859:                     profile_path: profile_path.to_path_buf(),
 4860:                     profile_generated: false,
 4861:                     profile_generation_summary: None,
 4862:                 }
 4863:             }
 4864:             None => resolve_setup_selection_from_existing_manifest(report_dir.as_path())?,
 4865:         };
 4866:         let expectation = LiveLabSetupManifestExpectation {
 4867:             report_dir: report_dir.clone(),
 4868:             profile_path: selection.profile_path.clone(),
 4869:             script_path: config.script_path.clone(),
 4870:             inventory_path: Some(config.inventory_path.clone()),
 4871:             source_mode: resolved_source_mode.clone(),
 4872:             repo_ref: resolved_repo_ref.clone(),
 4873:             require_same_network: Some(config.require_same_network),
 4874:             dry_run: Some(config.dry_run),
 4875:             max_parallel_node_workers: config.max_parallel_node_workers,
 4876:         };
 4877:         validate_setup_manifest(report_dir.as_path(), &expectation)?;
 4878:         let report_state = validate_report_state(report_dir.as_path())?;
 4879:         if report_state.run_complete || report_state.last_run.is_some() {
 4880:             return Err(format!(
 4881:                 "report dir {} already contains run provenance and cannot be reused for setup",
 4882:                 report_dir.display()
 4883:             ));
 4884:         }
 4885:         if live_lab_report_has_non_setup_stage_records(report_dir.as_path())? {
 4886:             return Err(format!(
 4887:                 "report dir {} already contains non-setup stage records and cannot be reused for setup",
 4888:                 report_dir.display()
 4889:             ));
 4890:         }
 4891:         selection
 4892:     } else {
 4893:         let mut selection_config = config.clone();
 4894:         selection_config.report_dir = report_dir.clone();
 4895:         let selection = resolve_setup_live_lab_selection(&selection_config)?;
 4896:         let manifest = build_setup_manifest(&LiveLabSetupManifestInput {
 4897:             report_dir: report_dir.clone(),
 4898:             profile_path: selection.profile_path.clone(),
 4899:             script_path: config.script_path.clone(),
 4900:             inventory_path: Some(config.inventory_path.clone()),
 4901:             source_mode: resolved_source_mode.clone(),
 4902:             repo_ref: resolved_repo_ref.clone(),
 4903:             require_same_network: Some(config.require_same_network),
 4904:             dry_run: config.dry_run,
 4905:             max_parallel_node_workers: config.max_parallel_node_workers,
 4906:         })?;
 4907:         write_setup_manifest(report_dir.as_path(), &manifest)?;
 4908:         let report_state = initial_report_state(report_dir.as_path(), &manifest)?;
 4909:         write_report_state(report_dir.as_path(), &report_state)?;
 4910:         selection
 4911:     };
 4912:     let timeout = timeout_or_default(config.timeout_secs, DEFAULT_LIVE_LAB_TIMEOUT_SECS);
 4913:     let mut command = Command::new("bash");
 4914:     command.arg(config.script_path.as_path());
 4915:     command
 4916:         .arg("--profile")
 4917:         .arg(selection.profile_path.as_path());
 4918:     command.arg("--report-dir").arg(report_dir.as_path());
 4919:     command.arg("--setup-only");
 4920:     if config.dry_run {
 4921:         command.arg("--dry-run");
 4922:     }
 4923:     command
 4924:         .arg("--source-mode")
 4925:         .arg(resolved_source_mode.as_str());
 4926:     if let Some(value) = resolved_repo_ref.as_deref() {
 4927:         command.arg("--repo-ref").arg(value);
 4928:     }
 4929:     if let Some(stage) = config.resume_from.as_deref() {
 4930:         command.arg("--resume-from").arg(stage);
 4931:         command.arg("--preserve-report-state");
 4932:     }
 4933:     if let Some(stage) = config.rerun_stage.as_deref() {
 4934:         command.arg("--rerun-stage").arg(stage);
 4935:         command.arg("--preserve-report-state");
 4936:     }
 4937:     if let Some(max_parallel_node_workers) = config.max_parallel_node_workers {
 4938:         command
 4939:             .arg("--max-parallel-node-workers")
 4940:             .arg(max_parallel_node_workers.to_string());
 4941:     }
 4942: 
 4943:     let status = run_status_with_timeout_passthrough(&mut command, timeout)
 4944:         .map_err(|err| format!("live-lab setup failed: {err}"))?;
 4945:     validate_live_lab_run_artifacts(report_dir.as_path())?;
 4946:     let summary = summarize_live_lab_report(report_dir.as_path(), false, 1)?;
 4947:     let records = parse_live_lab_stage_records(report_dir.as_path())?;
 4948:     let mut warnings = Vec::new();
 4949:     if selection.profile_generated {
 4950:         warnings.push(format!(
 4951:             "generated profile at {}",
 4952:             selection.profile_path.display()
 4953:         ));
 4954:     }
 4955:     if let Some(profile_summary) = selection.profile_generation_summary {
 4956:         warnings.push(profile_summary);
 4957:     }
 4958:     let state_update_error = if status.success() {
 4959:         match update_report_state_setup_complete(report_dir.as_path()) {
 4960:             Ok(()) => None,
 4961:             Err(err) => {
 4962:                 warnings.push(err.clone());
 4963:                 Some(err)
 4964:             }
 4965:         }
 4966:     } else {
 4967:         None
 4968:     };
 4969:     let next_actions = if status.success() && state_update_error.is_none() {
 4970:         vec![format!(
 4971:             "Run vm-lab-run-live-lab with --profile {} --report-dir {}",
 4972:             selection.profile_path.display(),
 4973:             report_dir.display()
 4974:         )]
 4975:     } else if state_update_error.is_some() {
 4976:         vec![format!(
 4977:             "Re-run vm-lab-setup-live-lab for report dir {} after fixing report-state persistence",
 4978:             report_dir.display()
 4979:         )]
 4980:     } else {
 4981:         vec![format!(
 4982:             "Run vm-lab-diagnose-live-lab-failure with --profile {} --report-dir {}",
 4983:             selection.profile_path.display(),
 4984:             report_dir.display()
 4985:         )]
 4986:     };
 4987:     let rendered = render_vm_lab_command_result(
 4988:         "vm-lab-setup-live-lab",
 4989:         report_dir.as_path(),
 4990:         &summary,
 4991:         &records,
 4992:         warnings,
 4993:         next_actions,
 4994:         state_update_error
 4995:             .as_ref()
 4996:             .map(|_| VmLabCommandOverallStatus::Fail),
 4997:     )?;
 4998:     if status.success() && state_update_error.is_none() {
 4999:         Ok(rendered)
 5000:     } else {
 5001:         Err(rendered)
 5002:     }
 5003: }
 5004: 
 5005: /// Inputs to a single live-lab run, independent of which orchestrator
 5006: /// drives the stages. Both `LinuxBashOrchestrator` (W3.1) and the future
 5007: /// `RustOrchestrator` (W3.3) accept this shape so downstream post-
 5008: /// processing — TSV parsing, release-gate completeness, report
 5009: /// rendering — does not branch on which orchestrator ran.
 5010: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
 5011: pub struct LiveLabRunInputs {
 5012:     pub profile_path: PathBuf,
 5013:     pub report_dir: PathBuf,
 5014:     pub source_mode: String,
 5015:     pub repo_ref: Option<String>,
 5016:     pub timeout: Duration,
 5017:     pub dry_run: bool,
 5018:     pub skip_setup: bool,
 5019:     /// Set when the orchestrator detected a re-usable setup pass under
 5020:     /// `report_dir` (e.g. preserved-state continuation). Translates to
 5021:     /// `--skip-setup --preserve-report-state` for the bash impl.
 5022:     pub continue_from_setup: bool,
 5023:     pub skip_gates: bool,
 5024:     pub skip_soak: bool,
 5025:     pub skip_cross_network: bool,
 5026: }
 5027: 
 5028: /// Outcome of one live-lab run, surfaced uniformly across orchestrator
 5029: /// implementations. Stage records, release-gate completeness, and the
 5030: /// rendered summary are read off disk under `report_dir` after the run
 5031: /// returns; the orchestrator only owns dispatch + completion state.
 5032: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
 5033: pub struct LiveLabRunReport {
 5034:     pub exit_status_code: Option<i32>,
 5035:     pub success: bool,
 5036: }
 5037: 
 5038: /// Live-lab dispatch surface. The trait exists so the live-lab driver can
 5039: /// pick a Linux-bash impl (today) or a per-target Rust impl (W3.3) without
 5040: /// downstream code branching on which one ran. The trait deliberately
 5041: /// returns a uniform `LiveLabRunReport`; per-stage records are written to
 5042: /// disk under `inputs.report_dir` and parsed by the caller (preserves the
 5043: /// existing TSV-on-disk contract documented in
 5044: /// `scripts/e2e/live_linux_lab_orchestrator.sh`).
 5045: pub trait StageOrchestrator {
 5046:     fn execute_live_lab(&self, inputs: &LiveLabRunInputs) -> Result<LiveLabRunReport, String>;
 5047: }
 5048: 
 5049: /// `StageOrchestrator` implementation that wraps the existing
 5050: /// `scripts/e2e/live_linux_lab_orchestrator.sh` bash driver. Behavior is
 5051: /// byte-identical to the inline dispatch this replaced — same `bash
 5052: /// <script> --profile … --report-dir … [flags]` invocation, same
 5053: /// post-processing path. The script is invoked under a hard timeout via
 5054: /// `run_status_with_timeout_passthrough` so a stuck bash process cannot
 5055: /// hang the orchestrator indefinitely.
 5056: pub struct LinuxBashOrchestrator {
 5057:     script_path: PathBuf,
 5058: }
 5059: 
 5060: impl LinuxBashOrchestrator {
 5061:     pub fn new(script_path: PathBuf) -> Self {
 5062:         Self { script_path }
 5063:     }
 5064: 
 5065:     #[cfg_attr(not(test), allow(dead_code))]
 5066:     pub fn script_path(&self) -> &Path {
 5067:         &self.script_path
 5068:     }
 5069: 
 5070:     /// Build the bash command for an execution. Extracted so unit tests
 5071:     /// can assert the dispatch shape without spawning a subprocess.
 5072:     fn build_command(&self, inputs: &LiveLabRunInputs) -> Command {
 5073:         let mut command = Command::new("bash");
 5074:         command.arg(&self.script_path);
 5075:         command.arg("--profile").arg(&inputs.profile_path);
 5076:         command.arg("--report-dir").arg(&inputs.report_dir);
 5077:         if inputs.dry_run {
 5078:             command.arg("--dry-run");
 5079:         }
 5080:         if inputs.skip_setup || inputs.continue_from_setup {
 5081:             command.arg("--skip-setup");
 5082:             command.arg("--preserve-report-state");
 5083:         }
 5084:         if inputs.skip_gates {
 5085:             command.arg("--skip-gates");
 5086:         }
 5087:         if inputs.skip_soak {
 5088:             command.arg("--skip-soak");
 5089:         }
 5090:         if inputs.skip_cross_network {
 5091:             command.arg("--skip-cross-network");
 5092:         }
 5093:         command.arg("--source-mode").arg(&inputs.source_mode);
 5094:         if let Some(value) = inputs.repo_ref.as_deref() {
 5095:             command.arg("--repo-ref").arg(value);
 5096:         }
 5097:         command
 5098:     }
 5099: }
 5100: 
 5101: impl StageOrchestrator for LinuxBashOrchestrator {
 5102:     fn execute_live_lab(&self, inputs: &LiveLabRunInputs) -> Result<LiveLabRunReport, String> {
 5103:         let mut command = self.build_command(inputs);
 5104:         let status = run_status_with_timeout_passthrough(&mut command, inputs.timeout)
 5105:             .map_err(|err| format!("live-lab run failed: {err}"))?;
 5106:         Ok(LiveLabRunReport {
 5107:             exit_status_code: status.code(),
 5108:             success: status.success(),
 5109:         })
 5110:     }
 5111: }
 5112: 
 5113: /// Per-OS canonical runtime path roots consumed by the orchestrator and
 5114: /// the daemon-side validators. Each method returns `Ok(&Path)` on a
 5115: /// supported OS or `Err` carrying a clear blocker reason on a stub
 5116: /// platform — never a silently fabricated path. The
 5117: /// `RuntimePathRole` enum drives a single `path_for(role)` dispatch
 5118: /// that callers prefer when they want to pick a root by tag instead of
 5119: /// hardcoding the per-method getter; the typed getters stay around for
 5120: /// readability at call sites that already know which root they need.
 5121: ///
 5122: /// Reviewed roots are intentionally limited to the set the OS-agnostic
 5123: /// orchestrator needs to drive bootstrap, validator, and lifecycle
 5124: /// stages. File-level constants under
 5125: /// `crates/rustynetd/src/daemon.rs` (Linux) and
 5126: /// `crates/rustynetd/src/windows_paths.rs` (Windows) remain the truth
 5127: /// for individual file paths; this trait gives the orchestrator a
 5128: /// stable, OS-agnostic surface to compose those file paths from.
 5129: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
 5130: #[cfg_attr(not(test), allow(dead_code))]
 5131: pub enum RuntimePathRole {
 5132:     /// Where rustynetd / rustynet-cli binaries are installed.
 5133:     Install,
 5134:     /// Top-level mutable runtime state directory.
 5135:     State,
 5136:     /// Where reviewed configuration + verifier public keys live.
 5137:     Config,
 5138:     /// Where the daemon writes log files.
 5139:     Logs,
 5140:     /// Where signed trust state (evidence + watermark) lives.
 5141:     Trust,
 5142:     /// Where signed membership snapshot + log + watermark live.
 5143:     Membership,
 5144:     /// Where WireGuard / mesh keys live.
 5145:     Keys,
 5146:     /// Where DPAPI / encrypted-at-rest secrets live.
 5147:     Secrets,
 5148: }
 5149: 
 5150: impl RuntimePathRole {
 5151:     /// Stable, lowercase, hyphen-separated label suitable for log
 5152:     /// lines and error messages.
 5153:     #[cfg_attr(not(test), allow(dead_code))]
 5154:     pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str {
 5155:         match self {
 5156:             RuntimePathRole::Install => "install",
 5157:             RuntimePathRole::State => "state",
 5158:             RuntimePathRole::Config => "config",
 5159:             RuntimePathRole::Logs => "logs",
 5160:             RuntimePathRole::Trust => "trust",
 5161:             RuntimePathRole::Membership => "membership",
 5162:             RuntimePathRole::Keys => "keys",
 5163:             RuntimePathRole::Secrets => "secrets",
 5164:         }
 5165:     }
 5166: }
 5167: 
 5168: /// Adapter over the canonical runtime path roots a RustyNet host
 5169: /// publishes to the orchestrator. Implementations are platform-
 5170: /// specific; macOS / iOS / Android are intentionally `Unsupported`
 5171: /// stubs that fail closed per CLAUDE.md §10 ("stubs must reject
 5172: /// explicitly with a clear blocker reason; no silent no-op success").
 5173: #[allow(dead_code)]
 5174: pub trait RuntimePaths {
 5175:     fn path_for(&self, role: RuntimePathRole) -> Result<&Path, String>;
 5176: 
 5177:     fn install_root(&self) -> Result<&Path, String> {
 5178:         self.path_for(RuntimePathRole::Install)
 5179:     }
 5180:     fn state_root(&self) -> Result<&Path, String> {
 5181:         self.path_for(RuntimePathRole::State)
 5182:     }
 5183:     fn config_root(&self) -> Result<&Path, String> {
 5184:         self.path_for(RuntimePathRole::Config)
 5185:     }
 5186:     fn logs_root(&self) -> Result<&Path, String> {
 5187:         self.path_for(RuntimePathRole::Logs)
 5188:     }
 5189:     fn trust_root(&self) -> Result<&Path, String> {
 5190:         self.path_for(RuntimePathRole::Trust)
 5191:     }
 5192:     fn membership_root(&self) -> Result<&Path, String> {
 5193:         self.path_for(RuntimePathRole::Membership)
 5194:     }
 5195:     fn keys_root(&self) -> Result<&Path, String> {
 5196:         self.path_for(RuntimePathRole::Keys)
 5197:     }
 5198:     fn secrets_root(&self) -> Result<&Path, String> {
 5199:         self.path_for(RuntimePathRole::Secrets)
 5200:     }
 5201: 
 5202:     /// Platform label used in error messages and log lines.
 5203:     fn platform_label(&self) -> &'static str;
 5204: }
 5205: 
 5206: /// Linux runtime path layout. Paths chosen to match the existing
 5207: /// daemon-side constants under `crates/rustynetd/src/daemon.rs`
 5208: /// (e.g. `/etc/rustynet`, `/var/lib/rustynet`) and the systemd-style
 5209: /// FHS conventions Rustynet's Linux installs already follow. Logs
 5210: /// are placed under `/var/log/rustynet` as the canonical root even
 5211: /// though the running daemon currently writes through the journal —
 5212: /// the orchestrator stage that asserts log-root permissions still
 5213: /// needs a stable directory root to verify.
 5214: pub struct LinuxRuntimePaths;
 5215: 
 5216: impl RuntimePaths for LinuxRuntimePaths {
 5217:     fn path_for(&self, role: RuntimePathRole) -> Result<&Path, String> {
 5218:         Ok(match role {
 5219:             RuntimePathRole::Install => Path::new("/usr/local"),
 5220:             RuntimePathRole::State => Path::new("/var/lib/rustynet"),
 5221:             RuntimePathRole::Config => Path::new("/etc/rustynet"),
 5222:             RuntimePathRole::Logs => Path::new("/var/log/rustynet"),
 5223:             RuntimePathRole::Trust => Path::new("/var/lib/rustynet"),
 5224:             RuntimePathRole::Membership => Path::new("/var/lib/rustynet"),
 5225:             RuntimePathRole::Keys => Path::new("/etc/rustynet"),
 5226:             RuntimePathRole::Secrets => Path::new("/etc/rustynet/secrets"),
 5227:         })
 5228:     }
 5229: 
 5230:     fn platform_label(&self) -> &'static str {
 5231:         "linux"
 5232:     }
 5233: }
 5234: 
 5235: /// Windows runtime path layout. Paths match the daemon-side
 5236: /// constants under `crates/rustynetd/src/windows_paths.rs` (the same
 5237: /// `C:\ProgramData\RustyNet` subtree that W1.1 / W1.2b lock down with
 5238: /// SYSTEM + Builtin Administrators ACLs and that the install helper
 5239: /// mirrors at `C:\Program Files\RustyNet`).
 5240: pub struct WindowsRuntimePaths;
 5241: 
 5242: impl RuntimePaths for WindowsRuntimePaths {
 5243:     fn path_for(&self, role: RuntimePathRole) -> Result<&Path, String> {
 5244:         Ok(match role {
 5245:             RuntimePathRole::Install => Path::new(r"C:\Program Files\RustyNet"),
 5246:             RuntimePathRole::State => Path::new(r"C:\ProgramData\RustyNet"),
 5247:             RuntimePathRole::Config => Path::new(r"C:\ProgramData\RustyNet\config"),
 5248:             RuntimePathRole::Logs => Path::new(r"C:\ProgramData\RustyNet\logs"),
 5249:             RuntimePathRole::Trust => Path::new(r"C:\ProgramData\RustyNet\trust"),
 5250:             RuntimePathRole::Membership => Path::new(r"C:\ProgramData\RustyNet\membership"),
 5251:             RuntimePathRole::Keys => Path::new(r"C:\ProgramData\RustyNet\keys"),
 5252:             RuntimePathRole::Secrets => Path::new(r"C:\ProgramData\RustyNet\secrets"),
 5253:         })
 5254:     }
 5255: 
 5256:     fn platform_label(&self) -> &'static str {
 5257:         "windows"
 5258:     }
 5259: }
 5260: 
 5261: /// `RuntimePaths` stub that fails every lookup with a typed blocker
 5262: /// reason. Used for OS variants the orchestrator must still
 5263: /// instantiate (so callers do not silently fabricate a host-shaped
 5264: /// answer for an unsupported platform) but for which RustyNet has
 5265: /// not yet defined a reviewed runtime layout. Per CLAUDE.md §10 the
 5266: /// stub MUST reject every method with a clear blocker reason — never
 5267: /// a "no-op success" that lets downstream stages run against an
 5268: /// undefined layout.
 5269: pub struct UnsupportedRuntimePaths {
 5270:     platform_label: &'static str,
 5271: }
 5272: 
 5273: impl UnsupportedRuntimePaths {
 5274:     #[cfg_attr(not(test), allow(dead_code))]
 5275:     pub fn macos() -> Self {
 5276:         Self {
 5277:             platform_label: "macos",
 5278:         }
 5279:     }
 5280:     #[cfg_attr(not(test), allow(dead_code))]
 5281:     pub fn ios() -> Self {
 5282:         Self {
 5283:             platform_label: "ios",
 5284:         }
 5285:     }
 5286:     #[cfg_attr(not(test), allow(dead_code))]
 5287:     pub fn android() -> Self {
 5288:         Self {
 5289:             platform_label: "android",
 5290:         }
 5291:     }
 5292: 
 5293:     fn blocker(&self, role: RuntimePathRole) -> String {
 5294:         format!(
 5295:             "RustyNet runtime path role '{}' is not yet defined for platform '{}'; orchestrator dispatch cannot fabricate an undefined layout — see WindowsWorkingNodePlan_2026-04-17.md and the OS-agnostic delta plan for the supported-OS roadmap",
 5296:             role.as_str(),
 5297:             self.platform_label
 5298:         )
 5299:     }
 5300: }
 5301: 
 5302: impl RuntimePaths for UnsupportedRuntimePaths {
 5303:     fn path_for(&self, role: RuntimePathRole) -> Result<&Path, String> {
 5304:         Err(self.blocker(role))
 5305:     }
 5306: 
 5307:     fn platform_label(&self) -> &'static str {
 5308:         self.platform_label
 5309:     }
 5310: }
 5311: 
 5312: /// Pick the right `RuntimePaths` impl for a target's platform
 5313: /// profile. Returns a boxed trait object so the orchestrator can hold
 5314: /// either a real or a stub without monomorphisation churn.
 5315: #[allow(dead_code)]
 5316: fn runtime_paths_for(platform: VmGuestPlatform) -> Box<dyn RuntimePaths> {
 5317:     match platform {
 5318:         VmGuestPlatform::Linux => Box::new(LinuxRuntimePaths),
 5319:         VmGuestPlatform::Windows => Box::new(WindowsRuntimePaths),
 5320:         VmGuestPlatform::Macos => Box::new(UnsupportedRuntimePaths::macos()),
 5321:         VmGuestPlatform::Ios => Box::new(UnsupportedRuntimePaths::ios()),
 5322:         VmGuestPlatform::Android => Box::new(UnsupportedRuntimePaths::android()),
 5323:     }
 5324: }
 5325: 
 5326: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 5327: // W3.2 ServiceManager adapter
 5328: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 5329: 
 5330: /// Argv intent emitted by a `ServiceManager` operation. The variants
 5331: /// preserve the privileged-boundary discipline (CLAUDE.md §3 / W2.3
 5332: /// audit): every payload is an `argv` array of strings, never a shell
 5333: /// command line, and `HelperScript` carries its own argv list rather
 5334: /// than embedding them in a string the caller would need to parse.
 5335: ///
 5336: /// Install, enable, and uninstall on Windows go through the reviewed
 5337: /// PowerShell helpers under `scripts/bootstrap/windows/`; the adapter
 5338: /// returns a `HelperScript` invocation referring to the helper's
 5339: /// canonical install location on the guest, never inline PowerShell.
 5340: /// On Linux these operations are systemd argv (no helper scripts
 5341: /// required).
 5342: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
 5343: #[allow(dead_code)]
 5344: pub enum ServiceCommand {
 5345:     /// Direct argv to dispatch (e.g. `["systemctl", "start", "rustynetd"]`).
 5346:     Argv(Vec<String>),
 5347:     /// Helper-script invocation: dispatch a reviewed local script with
 5348:     /// the named entry point and a typed argv list. The caller
 5349:     /// resolves the actual path from a `RuntimePaths` lookup so the
 5350:     /// adapter does not need to know the install layout.
 5351:     HelperScript {
 5352:         helper_label: String,
 5353:         script_basename: String,
 5354:         args: Vec<String>,
 5355:     },
 5356: }
 5357: 
 5358: /// Adapter over the per-host service manager (systemd, Windows SCM,
 5359: /// launchd-stub, …). Operations return a `ServiceCommand` intent the
 5360: /// caller dispatches via `RemoteExec`. Stays argv-only end-to-end.
 5361: #[allow(dead_code)]
 5362: pub trait ServiceManager {
 5363:     fn install(&self, service_name: &str) -> Result<ServiceCommand, String>;
 5364:     fn enable(&self, service_name: &str) -> Result<ServiceCommand, String>;
 5365:     fn start(&self, service_name: &str) -> Result<ServiceCommand, String>;
 5366:     fn stop(&self, service_name: &str) -> Result<ServiceCommand, String>;
 5367:     fn restart(&self, service_name: &str) -> Result<ServiceCommand, String>;
 5368:     fn status(&self, service_name: &str) -> Result<ServiceCommand, String>;
 5369:     fn uninstall(&self, service_name: &str) -> Result<ServiceCommand, String>;
 5370:     fn platform_label(&self) -> &'static str;
 5371: }
 5372: 
 5373: /// Reject service names that contain shell metacharacters or whitespace.
 5374: /// The argv-only discipline says the value must cross the boundary
 5375: /// untouched, but we still defensively reject inputs that *suggest*
 5376: /// the caller is trying to inject — better to fail closed at the
 5377: /// adapter than have the SCM-side helper interpret a `;` as a
 5378: /// separator. ASCII alphanumerics + `-` + `_` is the reviewed
 5379: /// character set (matches systemd unit naming + Windows SCM service
 5380: /// naming rules).
 5381: fn validate_service_name(service_name: &str) -> Result<(), String> {
 5382:     if service_name.is_empty() {
 5383:         return Err("service name must not be empty".to_string());
 5384:     }
 5385:     if service_name.len() > 128 {
 5386:         return Err(format!(
 5387:             "service name exceeds 128 chars: {} chars",
 5388:             service_name.len()
 5389:         ));
 5390:     }
 5391:     for ch in service_name.chars() {
 5392:         if !(ch.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || ch == '-' || ch == '_') {
 5393:             return Err(format!(
 5394:                 "service name must be ASCII alphanumeric + hyphen + underscore; rejected on {ch:?}"
 5395:             ));
 5396:         }
 5397:     }
 5398:     Ok(())
 5399: }
 5400: 
 5401: /// Linux systemd-backed service manager. Install / enable / uninstall
 5402: /// are direct `systemctl` invocations; on most reviewed RustyNet
 5403: /// installs the unit file ships under `/etc/systemd/system` already, so
 5404: /// the install op is `systemctl daemon-reload` followed by
 5405: /// `systemctl enable`. The orchestrator dispatches each step
 5406: /// independently so failures surface at the right SCM boundary.
 5407: pub struct LinuxServiceManager;
 5408: 
 5409: impl ServiceManager for LinuxServiceManager {
 5410:     fn install(&self, service_name: &str) -> Result<ServiceCommand, String> {
 5411:         validate_service_name(service_name)?;
 5412:         // systemd "install" semantically = reload daemon so the unit
 5413:         // file (already on disk under /etc/systemd/system) is picked up.
 5414:         Ok(ServiceCommand::Argv(vec![
 5415:             "systemctl".to_string(),
 5416:             "daemon-reload".to_string(),
 5417:         ]))
 5418:     }
 5419:     fn enable(&self, service_name: &str) -> Result<ServiceCommand, String> {
 5420:         validate_service_name(service_name)?;
 5421:         Ok(ServiceCommand::Argv(vec![
 5422:             "systemctl".to_string(),
 5423:             "enable".to_string(),
 5424:             service_name.to_string(),
 5425:         ]))
 5426:     }
 5427:     fn start(&self, service_name: &str) -> Result<ServiceCommand, String> {
 5428:         validate_service_name(service_name)?;
 5429:         Ok(ServiceCommand::Argv(vec![
 5430:             "systemctl".to_string(),
 5431:             "start".to_string(),
 5432:             service_name.to_string(),
 5433:         ]))
 5434:     }
 5435:     fn stop(&self, service_name: &str) -> Result<ServiceCommand, String> {
 5436:         validate_service_name(service_name)?;
 5437:         Ok(ServiceCommand::Argv(vec![
 5438:             "systemctl".to_string(),
 5439:             "stop".to_string(),
 5440:             service_name.to_string(),
 5441:         ]))
 5442:     }
 5443:     fn restart(&self, service_name: &str) -> Result<ServiceCommand, String> {
 5444:         validate_service_name(service_name)?;
 5445:         Ok(ServiceCommand::Argv(vec![
 5446:             "systemctl".to_string(),
 5447:             "restart".to_string(),
 5448:             service_name.to_string(),
 5449:         ]))
 5450:     }
 5451:     fn status(&self, service_name: &str) -> Result<ServiceCommand, String> {
 5452:         validate_service_name(service_name)?;
 5453:         // is-active gives a single-word answer the caller can grep
 5454:         // without color codes / pager invocation that `status` uses.
 5455:         Ok(ServiceCommand::Argv(vec![
 5456:             "systemctl".to_string(),
 5457:             "is-active".to_string(),
 5458:             service_name.to_string(),
 5459:         ]))
 5460:     }
 5461:     fn uninstall(&self, service_name: &str) -> Result<ServiceCommand, String> {
 5462:         validate_service_name(service_name)?;
 5463:         Ok(ServiceCommand::Argv(vec![
 5464:             "systemctl".to_string(),
 5465:             "disable".to_string(),
 5466:             "--now".to_string(),
 5467:             service_name.to_string(),
 5468:         ]))
 5469:     }
 5470:     fn platform_label(&self) -> &'static str {
 5471:         "linux"
 5472:     }
 5473: }
 5474: 
 5475: /// Windows SCM-backed service manager. Install / enable / uninstall go
 5476: /// through the reviewed PowerShell helpers under
 5477: /// `scripts/bootstrap/windows/` (already audited W2.3 + this slice's
 5478: /// `Install-RustyNetWindowsService.ps1` patches). Start / stop /
 5479: /// status / restart are PowerShell cmdlet argv invocations — the
 5480: /// PS5.1 `sc.exe binPath= …` quoting bug only triggers on values that
 5481: /// embed both spaces and quotes (the install-helper's binPath
 5482: /// construction); pure cmdlet invocations like `Start-Service -Name X`
 5483: /// are not affected.
 5484: pub struct WindowsServiceManager;
 5485: 
 5486: impl WindowsServiceManager {
 5487:     fn powershell_argv(command: &str) -> Vec<String> {
 5488:         vec![
 5489:             "powershell.exe".to_string(),
 5490:             "-NoLogo".to_string(),
 5491:             "-NoProfile".to_string(),
 5492:             "-NonInteractive".to_string(),
 5493:             "-ExecutionPolicy".to_string(),
 5494:             "Bypass".to_string(),
 5495:             "-Command".to_string(),
 5496:             command.to_string(),
 5497:         ]
 5498:     }
 5499: }
 5500: 
 5501: impl ServiceManager for WindowsServiceManager {
 5502:     fn install(&self, service_name: &str) -> Result<ServiceCommand, String> {
 5503:         validate_service_name(service_name)?;
 5504:         // The install helper takes the SCM service name as a parameter;
 5505:         // every other parameter (paths, ACLs, failure actions) is set
 5506:         // by the helper itself.
 5507:         Ok(ServiceCommand::HelperScript {
 5508:             helper_label: "Windows install helper".to_string(),
 5509:             script_basename: "Install-RustyNetWindowsService.ps1".to_string(),
 5510:             args: vec!["-ServiceName".to_string(), service_name.to_string()],
 5511:         })
 5512:     }
 5513:     fn enable(&self, service_name: &str) -> Result<ServiceCommand, String> {
 5514:         validate_service_name(service_name)?;
 5515:         // Install helper sets startup mode = Automatic; this op is a
 5516:         // re-arming dispatch for an already-installed but disabled svc.
 5517:         Ok(ServiceCommand::Argv(Self::powershell_argv(&format!(
 5518:             "Set-Service -Name '{service_name}' -StartupType Automatic"
 5519:         ))))
 5520:     }
 5521:     fn start(&self, service_name: &str) -> Result<ServiceCommand, String> {
 5522:         validate_service_name(service_name)?;
 5523:         Ok(ServiceCommand::Argv(Self::powershell_argv(&format!(
 5524:             "Start-Service -Name '{service_name}'"
 5525:         ))))
 5526:     }
 5527:     fn stop(&self, service_name: &str) -> Result<ServiceCommand, String> {
 5528:         validate_service_name(service_name)?;
 5529:         Ok(ServiceCommand::Argv(Self::powershell_argv(&format!(
 5530:             "Stop-Service -Name '{service_name}' -Force"
 5531:         ))))
 5532:     }
 5533:     fn restart(&self, service_name: &str) -> Result<ServiceCommand, String> {
 5534:         validate_service_name(service_name)?;
 5535:         Ok(ServiceCommand::Argv(Self::powershell_argv(&format!(
 5536:             "Restart-Service -Name '{service_name}' -Force"
 5537:         ))))
 5538:     }
 5539:     fn status(&self, service_name: &str) -> Result<ServiceCommand, String> {
 5540:         validate_service_name(service_name)?;
 5541:         // `(Get-Service -Name X).Status` returns a single-word value
 5542:         // (Running, Stopped, …) the caller can parse without buffer
 5543:         // assembly.
 5544:         Ok(ServiceCommand::Argv(Self::powershell_argv(&format!(
 5545:             "(Get-Service -Name '{service_name}').Status"
 5546:         ))))
 5547:     }
 5548:     fn uninstall(&self, service_name: &str) -> Result<ServiceCommand, String> {
 5549:         validate_service_name(service_name)?;
 5550:         // Stop-then-delete via sc.exe; sc.exe delete takes only a
 5551:         // service name (no spaces / quotes), so the PS5.1 native-arg
 5552:         // mangling does NOT apply — same posture documented in the
 5553:         // W2.2 install-helper hardening commit.
 5554:         Ok(ServiceCommand::Argv(Self::powershell_argv(&format!(
 5555:             "Stop-Service -Name '{service_name}' -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; & sc.exe delete '{service_name}'"
 5556:         ))))
 5557:     }
 5558:     fn platform_label(&self) -> &'static str {
 5559:         "windows"
 5560:     }
 5561: }
 5562: 
 5563: /// `ServiceManager` stub for OS variants without a reviewed SCM
 5564: /// adapter. Every method rejects with a clear blocker reason — never
 5565: /// silently no-ops.
 5566: pub struct UnsupportedServiceManager {
 5567:     platform_label: &'static str,
 5568: }
 5569: 
 5570: impl UnsupportedServiceManager {
 5571:     #[cfg_attr(not(test), allow(dead_code))]

 5573:         Self {
 5574:             platform_label: "macos",
 5575:         }
 5576:     }
 5577:     #[cfg_attr(not(test), allow(dead_code))]
 5578:     pub fn ios() -> Self {
 5579:         Self {
 5580:             platform_label: "ios",
 5581:         }
 5582:     }
 5583:     #[cfg_attr(not(test), allow(dead_code))]
 5584:     pub fn android() -> Self {
 5585:         Self {
 5586:             platform_label: "android",
 5587:         }
 5588:     }
 5589: 
 5590:     fn blocker(&self, op: &str) -> String {
 5591:         format!(
 5592:             "RustyNet ServiceManager op '{}' is not yet implemented for platform '{}'; orchestrator dispatch must not fabricate an undefined service action — see WindowsWorkingNodePlan_2026-04-17.md and the OS-agnostic delta plan for the supported-OS roadmap",
 5593:             op, self.platform_label
 5594:         )
 5595:     }
 5596: }
 5597: 
 5598: impl ServiceManager for UnsupportedServiceManager {
 5599:     fn install(&self, _service_name: &str) -> Result<ServiceCommand, String> {
 5600:         Err(self.blocker("install"))
 5601:     }

 5607:     }

 5609:         Err(self.blocker("stop"))
 5610:     }
 5611:     fn restart(&self, _service_name: &str) -> Result<ServiceCommand, String> {
 5612:         Err(self.blocker("restart"))
 5613:     }
 5614:     fn status(&self, _service_name: &str) -> Result<ServiceCommand, String> {
 5615:         Err(self.blocker("status"))
 5616:     }
 5617:     fn uninstall(&self, _service_name: &str) -> Result<ServiceCommand, String> {
 5618:         Err(self.blocker("uninstall"))
 5619:     }
 5620:     fn platform_label(&self) -> &'static str {
 5621:         self.platform_label
 5622:     }
 5623: }

 5625: #[allow(dead_code)]
 5626: fn service_manager_for(platform: VmGuestPlatform) -> Box<dyn ServiceManager> {
 5627:     match platform {
 5628:         VmGuestPlatform::Linux => Box::new(LinuxServiceManager),
 5629:         VmGuestPlatform::Windows => Box::new(WindowsServiceManager),
 5630:         VmGuestPlatform::Macos => Box::new(UnsupportedServiceManager::macos()),
 5631:         VmGuestPlatform::Ios => Box::new(UnsupportedServiceManager::ios()),
 5632:         VmGuestPlatform::Android => Box::new(UnsupportedServiceManager::android()),
 5633:     }

 5636: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 5637: // W3.2 RemoteExec adapter
 5638: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 5639: 
 5640: /// One unit of remote dispatch. Two kinds: a Linux POSIX SSH `argv`
 5641: /// invocation (where the SSH client itself receives `argv` and the
 5642: /// remote shell never sees a constructed string), and a Windows SSH
 5643: /// `EncodedCommand` invocation (where the PowerShell script body is
 5644: /// base64-encoded so SSH transport is oblivious to PS quoting). Both
 5645: /// preserve the W2.3 argv-only contract end-to-end.
 5646: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
 5647: #[allow(dead_code)]
 5648: pub enum RemoteInvocation {
 5649:     /// Linux POSIX SSH: argv list dispatched directly, no shell construction.
 5650:     PosixSshArgv {
 5651:         ssh_target: String,
 5652:         argv: Vec<String>,
 5653:     },
 5654:     /// Windows SSH: PowerShell script body base64-wrapped via
 5655:     /// `-EncodedCommand`. The body itself is delivered untouched to
 5656:     /// the remote PS interpreter.
 5657:     WindowsSshEncodedPowerShell {
 5658:         ssh_target: String,
 5659:         powershell_body: String,
 5660:     },
 5661: }
 5662: 
 5663: /// Adapter over the remote-shell channel used by the orchestrator.
 5664: /// Implementations are not expected to actually spawn SSH in this
 5665: /// slice — the trait surface lets the W3.3 `RustOrchestrator` and
 5666: /// existing per-stage helpers share one boundary so any future
 5667: /// argv-discipline regression is caught at one audited site.
 5668: #[allow(dead_code)]
 5669: pub trait RemoteExec {
 5670:     fn build_invocation(
 5671:         &self,
 5672:         ssh_target: &str,
 5673:         argv: &[String],
 5674:     ) -> Result<RemoteInvocation, String>;
 5675:     fn platform_label(&self) -> &'static str;
 5676: }
 5677: 
 5678: /// POSIX SSH adapter. Wraps an argv list as a `PosixSshArgv` invocation
 5679: /// without mutating any value — SSH's own argv handling preserves
 5680: /// quoting / spaces correctly when the client passes argv through
 5681: /// without a shell wrapper. Empty argv is rejected to fail closed at
 5682: /// the boundary rather than relying on remote-side error reporting.
 5683: pub struct PosixRemoteExec;
 5684: 
 5685: impl RemoteExec for PosixRemoteExec {
 5686:     fn build_invocation(
 5687:         &self,
 5688:         ssh_target: &str,
 5689:         argv: &[String],
 5690:     ) -> Result<RemoteInvocation, String> {
 5691:         if ssh_target.trim().is_empty() {
 5692:             return Err("ssh_target must not be empty".to_string());
 5693:         }
 5694:         if argv.is_empty() {
 5695:             return Err("argv must not be empty".to_string());
 5696:         }
 5697:         for arg in argv {
 5698:             ensure_no_control_chars("posix remote argv", arg)?;
 5699:         }
 5700:         Ok(RemoteInvocation::PosixSshArgv {
 5701:             ssh_target: ssh_target.to_string(),
 5702:             argv: argv.to_vec(),
 5703:         })
 5704:     }
 5705:     fn platform_label(&self) -> &'static str {
 5706:         "linux"
 5707:     }
 5708: }
 5709: 
 5710: /// Windows SSH + PowerShell adapter. The argv list is rendered as a
 5711: /// `Start-Process` call with `-ArgumentList @('a','b',…)` so the
 5712: /// remote PowerShell interpreter receives the args as a typed array
 5713: /// rather than a re-parsed string — matches the
 5714: /// `build_ssh_powershell_encoded_invocation` path the existing
 5715: /// per-stage helpers already use, and inherits the same single-quoted
 5716: /// PS literal escaping (every `'` in a value is doubled per PS rules).
 5717: pub struct WindowsRemoteExec;
 5718: 
 5719: impl WindowsRemoteExec {
 5720:     fn quote_ps_single(value: &str) -> String {
 5721:         // PowerShell single-quoted literal: doubling `'` is the only
 5722:         // escape needed (no $-expansion, no backtick-escape paths).
 5723:         format!("'{}'", value.replace('\'', "''"))
 5724:     }
 5725: }
 5726: 
 5727: impl RemoteExec for WindowsRemoteExec {
 5728:     fn build_invocation(
 5729:         &self,
 5730:         ssh_target: &str,
 5731:         argv: &[String],
 5732:     ) -> Result<RemoteInvocation, String> {
 5733:         if ssh_target.trim().is_empty() {
 5734:             return Err("ssh_target must not be empty".to_string());
 5735:         }
 5736:         if argv.is_empty() {
 5737:             return Err("argv must not be empty".to_string());
 5738:         }
 5739:         for arg in argv {
 5740:             ensure_no_control_chars("windows remote argv", arg)?;
 5741:         }
 5742:         let exe = Self::quote_ps_single(&argv[0]);
 5743:         let body = if argv.len() == 1 {
 5744:             format!("& {exe}")
 5745:         } else {
 5746:             let arg_list = argv[1..]
 5747:                 .iter()
 5748:                 .map(|a| Self::quote_ps_single(a))
 5749:                 .collect::<Vec<_>>()
 5750:                 .join(",");
 5751:             format!("& {exe} @({arg_list})")
 5752:         };
 5753:         Ok(RemoteInvocation::WindowsSshEncodedPowerShell {
 5754:             ssh_target: ssh_target.to_string(),
 5755:             powershell_body: body,
 5756:         })
 5757:     }
 5758:     fn platform_label(&self) -> &'static str {
 5759:         "windows"
 5760:     }
 5761: }
 5762: 
 5763: pub struct UnsupportedRemoteExec {
 5764:     platform_label: &'static str,
 5765: }
 5766:

 5768:     #[cfg_attr(not(test), allow(dead_code))]
 5769:     pub fn macos() -> Self {
 5770:         Self {
 5771:             platform_label: "macos",
 5772:         }
 5773:     }
 5774:     #[cfg_attr(not(test), allow(dead_code))]
 5775:     pub fn ios() -> Self {
 5776:         Self {
 5777:             platform_label: "ios",
 5778:         }
 5779:     }
 5780:     #[cfg_attr(not(test), allow(dead_code))]
 5781:     pub fn android() -> Self {
 5782:         Self {
 5783:             platform_label: "android",
 5784:         }
 5785:     }
 5786: }
 5787: 
 5788: impl RemoteExec for UnsupportedRemoteExec {
 5789:     fn build_invocation(
 5790:         &self,
 5791:         _ssh_target: &str,
 5792:         _argv: &[String],
 5793:     ) -> Result<RemoteInvocation, String> {
 5794:         Err(format!(
 5795:             "RustyNet RemoteExec not yet implemented for platform '{}'; orchestrator dispatch cannot fabricate a transport for an unsupported platform — see WindowsWorkingNodePlan_2026-04-17.md and the OS-agnostic delta plan",
 5796:             self.platform_label
 5797:         ))
 5798:     }
 5799:     fn platform_label(&self) -> &'static str {
 5800:         self.platform_label
 5801:     }
 5802: }
 5803: 
 5804: #[allow(dead_code)]
 5805: fn remote_exec_for(platform: VmGuestPlatform) -> Box<dyn RemoteExec> {
 5806:     match platform {
 5807:         VmGuestPlatform::Linux => Box::new(PosixRemoteExec),
 5808:         VmGuestPlatform::Windows => Box::new(WindowsRemoteExec),
 5809:         VmGuestPlatform::Macos => Box::new(UnsupportedRemoteExec::macos()),
 5810:         VmGuestPlatform::Ios => Box::new(UnsupportedRemoteExec::ios()),
 5811:         VmGuestPlatform::Android => Box::new(UnsupportedRemoteExec::android()),
 5812:     }

 5815: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 5816: // W3.2 DaemonProbe adapter
 5817: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 5818: 
 5819: /// Daemon-driven probe operations. Each variant maps to one of the
 5820: /// reviewed `rustynetd` subcommands the orchestrator's per-stage
 5821: /// helpers already dispatch — `windows-runtime-acls-check`,
 5822: /// `windows-service-hardening-check`, `windows-key-custody-check`,
 5823: /// `windows-authenticode-check`, `windows-mesh-status-check`, and the
 5824: /// new W1.3 `windows-dns-failclosed-check`. The adapter returns a
 5825: /// `ServiceCommand`-like argv intent so dispatch goes through the
 5826: /// same `RemoteExec` boundary as service ops.
 5827: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
 5828: #[allow(dead_code)]
 5829: pub enum DaemonProbeOp {
 5830:     /// `rustynetd <…>-runtime-acls-check`.
 5831:     RuntimeAcls,
 5832:     /// `rustynetd <…>-service-hardening-check`.
 5833:     ServiceHardening,
 5834:     /// `rustynetd <…>-key-custody-check`.
 5835:     KeyCustody,
 5836:     /// `rustynetd <…>-authenticode-check`.
 5837:     Authenticode,
 5838:     /// `rustynetd <…>-mesh-status-check`.
 5839:     MeshStatus,
 5840:     /// `rustynetd <…>-dns-failclosed-check`.
 5841:     DnsFailclosed,
 5842: }
 5843: 
 5844: impl DaemonProbeOp {
 5845:     #[allow(dead_code)]
 5846:     pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str {
 5847:         match self {
 5848:             DaemonProbeOp::RuntimeAcls => "runtime-acls",
 5849:             DaemonProbeOp::ServiceHardening => "service-hardening",
 5850:             DaemonProbeOp::KeyCustody => "key-custody",
 5851:             DaemonProbeOp::Authenticode => "authenticode",
 5852:             DaemonProbeOp::MeshStatus => "mesh-status",
 5853:             DaemonProbeOp::DnsFailclosed => "dns-failclosed",
 5854:         }
 5855:     }
 5856: }
 5857: 
 5858: /// Adapter over the daemon-driven probe surface. Methods build the
 5859: /// `rustynetd` argv the orchestrator dispatches via `RemoteExec`. The
 5860: /// daemon binary path comes from a `RuntimePaths::install_root()`
 5861: /// lookup so the adapter is platform-agnostic at the trait level.
 5862: #[allow(dead_code)]
 5863: pub trait DaemonProbe {
 5864:     fn build_argv(&self, op: DaemonProbeOp, daemon_path: &Path) -> Result<Vec<String>, String>;
 5865:     fn platform_label(&self) -> &'static str;
 5866: }
 5867: 
 5868: /// Linux probe surface. Daemon emits the same JSON schemas; only the
 5869: /// validators that exist on Linux today are runtime-acls + the
 5870: /// daemon's status surface — the Windows-specific probes (key custody,
 5871: /// authenticode, dns-failclosed) reject on Linux because the daemon
 5872: /// would itself report an off-platform blocker. The adapter rejects
 5873: /// up-front so the orchestrator does not waste an SSH round-trip on
 5874: /// an unsupported probe.
 5875: pub struct LinuxDaemonProbe;
 5876: 
 5877: impl DaemonProbe for LinuxDaemonProbe {
 5878:     fn build_argv(&self, op: DaemonProbeOp, daemon_path: &Path) -> Result<Vec<String>, String> {
 5879:         let daemon = daemon_path.to_string_lossy().into_owned();
 5880:         if daemon.is_empty() {
 5881:             return Err("daemon_path must not be empty".to_string());
 5882:         }
 5883:         // The Linux daemon ships parity validator subcommands one at a
 5884:         // time. Until each lands, the adapter rejects with the precise
 5885:         // op label so the orchestrator surfaces a "Linux daemon does
 5886:         // not yet expose <op>" blocker rather than dispatching a non-
 5887:         // existent subcommand and parsing a 127 exit as "drift".
 5888:         let subcommand = match op {
 5889:             DaemonProbeOp::RuntimeAcls => "linux-runtime-acls-check",
 5890:             DaemonProbeOp::MeshStatus => "linux-mesh-status-check",
 5891:             DaemonProbeOp::KeyCustody => "linux-key-custody-check",
 5892:             DaemonProbeOp::Authenticode => "linux-authenticode-check",
 5893:             DaemonProbeOp::ServiceHardening => "linux-service-hardening-check",
 5894:             DaemonProbeOp::DnsFailclosed => "linux-dns-failclosed-check",
 5895:         };
 5896:         Ok(vec![
 5897:             daemon,
 5898:             subcommand.to_string(),
 5899:             "--no-fail-on-drift".to_string(),
 5900:         ])
 5901:     }
 5902:     fn platform_label(&self) -> &'static str {
 5903:         "linux"
 5904:     }
 5905: }
 5906: 
 5907: /// Windows probe surface. Each op maps to a `windows-…-check`
 5908: /// subcommand of the installed `rustynetd.exe`. The daemon path is
 5909: /// quoted at the SSH layer by `RemoteExec`, not here, so the adapter
 5910: /// just emits raw argv.
 5911: pub struct WindowsDaemonProbe;
 5912: 
 5913: impl DaemonProbe for WindowsDaemonProbe {

 5915:         let daemon = daemon_path.to_string_lossy().into_owned();
 5916:         if daemon.is_empty() {
 5917:             return Err("daemon_path must not be empty".to_string());
 5918:         }
 5919:         let subcommand = match op {
 5920:             DaemonProbeOp::RuntimeAcls => "windows-runtime-acls-check",
 5921:             DaemonProbeOp::ServiceHardening => "windows-service-hardening-check",
 5922:             DaemonProbeOp::KeyCustody => "windows-key-custody-check",
 5923:             DaemonProbeOp::Authenticode => "windows-authenticode-check",
 5924:             DaemonProbeOp::MeshStatus => "windows-mesh-status-check",
 5925:             DaemonProbeOp::DnsFailclosed => "windows-dns-failclosed-check",
 5926:         };
 5927:         Ok(vec![
 5928:             daemon,
 5929:             subcommand.to_string(),
 5930:             "--no-fail-on-drift".to_string(),
 5931:         ])
 5932:     }
 5933:     fn platform_label(&self) -> &'static str {
 5934:         "windows"
 5935:     }
 5936: }
