 8594: /// Path of the installed `rustynetd.exe` on Windows guests, mirroring
 8595: /// `crate::windows_paths::DEFAULT_WINDOWS_INSTALL_ROOT` from the daemon.
 8596: const WINDOWS_RUSTYNETD_EXE_PATH: &str = r"C:\Program Files\RustyNet\rustynetd.exe";
 8597: 
 8598: /// Build the PowerShell script body that invokes one of the security-check
 8599: /// subcommands on the live Windows guest. Centralizes argv-only discipline so
 8600: /// every stage helper goes through the same audited path: the binary path and
 8601: /// every additional argument is quoted via `powershell_quote`, the subcommand
 8602: /// name and well-formed flags pass through unquoted, and any value carrying a
 8603: /// PowerShell metacharacter or control byte is rejected at construction.
 8604: fn build_windows_security_check_invocation(
 8605:     subcommand: &str,
 8606:     extra_args: &[String],
 8607: ) -> Result<String, String> {
 8608:     ensure_no_control_chars("Windows security-check subcommand", subcommand)?;
 8609:     if subcommand.is_empty()
 8610:         || !subcommand
 8611:             .chars()
 8612:             .all(|ch| ch.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || ch == '-')
 8613:     {
 8614:         return Err(format!(
 8615:             "Windows security-check subcommand must be ASCII-alphanumeric+hyphen: {subcommand:?}"
 8616:         ));
 8617:     }
 8618:     let mut script = format!(
 8619:         "& {exe} {subcommand} --no-fail-on-drift",
 8620:         exe = powershell_quote(WINDOWS_RUSTYNETD_EXE_PATH)?,
 8621:     );
 8622:     for arg in extra_args {
 8623:         ensure_no_control_chars("Windows security-check arg", arg.as_str())?;
 8624:         script.push(' ');
 8625:         if arg.starts_with("--")
 8626:             && arg
 8627:                 .chars()
 8628:                 .skip(2)
 8629:                 .all(|ch| ch.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || ch == '-')
 8630:         {
 8631:             // Well-formed long-flag: alphanumeric/hyphen only after `--`.
 8632:             // Safe to emit unquoted (PowerShell parser treats these as tokens).
 8633:             script.push_str(arg.as_str());
 8634:         } else {
 8635:             script.push_str(powershell_quote(arg.as_str())?.as_str());
 8636:         }
 8637:     }
 8638:     Ok(script)
 8639: }
 8640: 
 8641: fn run_validate_windows_runtime_acls_stage(
 8642:     windows_alias: &str,
 8643:     inventory_path: &Path,
 8644:     ssh_identity_file: &Path,
 8645:     known_hosts_path: Option<&Path>,
 8646: ) -> Result<(String, String), (String, String)> {
 8647:     let targets = resolve_remote_targets(inventory_path, &[windows_alias.to_string()], false, &[])
 8648:         .map_err(|err| (err, String::new()))?;
 8649:     let target = targets.into_iter().next().ok_or_else(|| {
 8650:         (
 8651:             format!("no target resolved for alias {windows_alias}"),
 8652:             String::new(),
 8653:         )
 8654:     })?;
 8655:     if target.platform_profile.platform != VmGuestPlatform::Windows {
 8656:         return Err((
 8657:             format!(
 8658:                 "alias {windows_alias} resolved to non-Windows platform: {}",
 8659:                 target.platform_profile.platform.as_str()
 8660:             ),
 8661:             String::new(),
 8662:         ));
 8663:     }
 8664:     let timeout = timeout_or_default(0, DEFAULT_RUN_TIMEOUT_SECS);
 8665:     let script = build_windows_security_check_invocation("windows-runtime-acls-check", &[])
 8666:         .map_err(|err| (err, String::new()))?;
 8667:     let invocation = build_ssh_powershell_encoded_invocation(script.as_str())
 8668:         .map_err(|err| (err, String::new()))?;
 8669:     let raw_output = capture_remote_shell_command_for_target(
 8670:         &target,
 8671:         None,
 8672:         Some(ssh_identity_file),
 8673:         known_hosts_path,
 8674:         invocation.as_str(),
 8675:         timeout,
 8676:     )
 8677:     .map_err(|err| {
 8678:         (
 8679:             format!("remote dispatch of windows-runtime-acls-check failed: {err}"),
 8680:             String::new(),
 8681:         )
 8682:     })?;
 8683:     let raw_trimmed = raw_output.trim().to_string();
 8684:     evaluate_windows_runtime_acls_report(windows_alias, raw_trimmed.as_str())
 8685:         .map(|summary| (summary, raw_trimmed.clone()))
 8686:         .map_err(|reason| (reason, raw_trimmed))
 8687: }
 8688: 
 8689: /// Pure evaluator for the JSON output of
 8690: /// `rustynetd windows-runtime-acls-check`. Returns a one-line success summary
 8691: /// or a precise drift reason. Callable in tests without SSH/IO.
 8692: fn evaluate_windows_runtime_acls_report(
 8693:     windows_alias: &str,
 8694:     raw_json: &str,
 8695: ) -> Result<String, String> {
 8696:     let report: rustynetd::windows_paths::WindowsRuntimeAclReport = serde_json::from_str(raw_json)
 8697:         .map_err(|err| format!("parse windows-runtime-acls-check JSON output failed: {err}"))?;
 8698:     if report.schema_version != 1 {
 8699:         return Err(format!(
 8700:             "windows-runtime-acls-check returned unsupported schema_version={}",
 8701:             report.schema_version
 8702:         ));
 8703:     }
 8704:     if report.roots.is_empty() {
 8705:         return Err(
 8706:             "windows-runtime-acls-check returned an empty roots list; expected the canonical \
 8707:              Windows runtime root set"
 8708:                 .to_string(),
 8709:         );
 8710:     }
 8711:     if !report.overall_ok {
 8712:         let drifted = report
 8713:             .roots
 8714:             .iter()
 8715:             .filter_map(|entry| match &entry.status {
 8716:                 rustynetd::windows_paths::WindowsRuntimeAclRootStatus::Ok => None,
 8717:                 rustynetd::windows_paths::WindowsRuntimeAclRootStatus::Missing { reason } => {
 8718:                     Some(format!("{} missing: {reason}", entry.label))
 8719:                 }
 8720:                 rustynetd::windows_paths::WindowsRuntimeAclRootStatus::Drifted { reason } => {
 8721:                     Some(format!("{} drifted: {reason}", entry.label))
 8722:                 }
 8723:             })
 8724:             .collect::<Vec<_>>();
 8725:         let drifted_summary = if drifted.is_empty() {
 8726:             "report set overall_ok=false but every per-root entry is Ok; output is inconsistent"
 8727:                 .to_string()
 8728:         } else {
 8729:             drifted.join("; ")
 8730:         };
 8731:         return Err(format!(
 8732:             "Windows runtime ACL drift detected: {drifted_summary}"
 8733:         ));
 8734:     }
 8735:     if report.roots.iter().any(|entry| {
 8736:         !matches!(
 8737:             entry.status,
 8738:             rustynetd::windows_paths::WindowsRuntimeAclRootStatus::Ok
 8739:         )
 8740:     }) {
 8741:         return Err(
 8742:             "report set overall_ok=true but at least one per-root entry is not Ok; output is \
 8743:              inconsistent"
 8744:                 .to_string(),
 8745:         );
 8746:     }
 8747:     let inspected_count = report.roots.len();
 8748:     Ok(format!(
 8749:         "Windows runtime ACLs verified on {windows_alias}: {inspected_count} reviewed roots passed"
 8750:     ))
 8751: }
 8752:

 8801: /// Pure evaluator for the JSON output of
 8802: /// `rustynetd windows-service-hardening-check`. Returns a one-line success
 8803: /// summary or a precise drift reason. Callable in tests without SSH/IO.
 8804: fn evaluate_windows_service_hardening_report(
 8805:     windows_alias: &str,
 8806:     raw_json: &str,
 8807: ) -> Result<String, String> {
 8808:     let report: rustynetd::windows_service_hardening::WindowsServiceHardeningReport =
 8809:         serde_json::from_str(raw_json).map_err(|err| {
 8810:             format!("parse windows-service-hardening-check JSON output failed: {err}")
 8811:         })?;
 8812:     if report.schema_version != 1 {
 8813:         return Err(format!(
 8814:             "windows-service-hardening-check returned unsupported schema_version={}",
 8815:             report.schema_version
 8816:         ));
 8817:     }
 8818:     if !report.overall_ok {
 8819:         let reasons = if report.drift_reasons.is_empty() {
 8820:             "report set overall_ok=false but no drift_reasons recorded; output is inconsistent"
 8821:                 .to_string()
 8822:         } else {
 8823:             report.drift_reasons.join("; ")
 8824:         };
 8825:         return Err(format!(
 8826:             "Windows service hardening drift detected: {reasons}"
 8827:         ));
 8828:     }
 8829:     if !report.drift_reasons.is_empty() {
 8830:         return Err(format!(
 8831:             "report set overall_ok=true but drift_reasons is non-empty: {}",
 8832:             report.drift_reasons.join("; ")
 8833:         ));
 8834:     }
 8835:     Ok(format!(
 8836:         "Windows service hardening verified on {windows_alias} (service={}, sid_type={}, failure_actions={})",
 8837:         report.snapshot.service_name,
 8838:         report.snapshot.service_sid_type,
 8839:         report.snapshot.failure_action_count
 8840:     ))
 8841: }

 8987: /// Pure evaluator for the JSON output of `rustynetd windows-authenticode-check`.
 8988: fn evaluate_windows_authenticode_report(
 8989:     windows_alias: &str,
 8990:     raw_json: &str,
 8991: ) -> Result<String, String> {
 8992:     let report: rustynetd::windows_authenticode::WindowsAuthenticodeReport =
 8993:         serde_json::from_str(raw_json)
 8994:             .map_err(|err| format!("parse windows-authenticode-check JSON output failed: {err}"))?;
 8995:     if report.schema_version != 1 {
 8996:         return Err(format!(
 8997:             "windows-authenticode-check returned unsupported schema_version={}",
 8998:             report.schema_version
 8999:         ));
 9000:     }
 9001:     if !report.overall_ok {
 9002:         let reasons = if report.drift_reasons.is_empty() {
 9003:             "report set overall_ok=false but no drift_reasons recorded; output is inconsistent"
 9004:                 .to_string()
 9005:         } else {
 9006:             report.drift_reasons.join("; ")
 9007:         };
 9008:         return Err(format!(
 9009:             "Windows Authenticode signature drift detected: {reasons}"
 9010:         ));
 9011:     }
 9012:     if !report.signature_present {
 9013:         return Err(format!(
 9014:             "Windows Authenticode report marked overall_ok=true but signature_present=false for {}; output is inconsistent",
 9015:             report.binary_path
 9016:         ));
 9017:     }
 9018:     // W2.1b: overall_ok=true MUST imply chain_status=Verified. The
 9019:     // daemon-side `inspect_authenticode_signature` enforces this
 9020:     // invariant; the orchestrator double-checks because a stale or
 9021:     // crafted JSON payload could try to claim overall_ok=true with a
 9022:     // weaker chain status.
 9023:     if !matches!(
 9024:         report.chain_status,
 9025:         rustynetd::windows_authenticode::WindowsAuthenticodeChainStatus::Verified
 9026:     ) {
 9027:         return Err(format!(
 9028:             "Windows Authenticode report marked overall_ok=true but chain_status is not 'verified' for {}; output is inconsistent",
 9029:             report.binary_path
 9030:         ));
 9031:     }
 9032:     if !report.drift_reasons.is_empty() {
 9033:         return Err(format!(
 9034:             "report set overall_ok=true but drift_reasons is non-empty: {}",
 9035:             report.drift_reasons.join("; ")
 9036:         ));
 9037:     }
 9038:     Ok(format!(
 9039:         "Windows Authenticode signature + chain verified on {windows_alias} ({}, {} certificate entries, {} bytes)",
 9040:         report.binary_path,
 9041:         report.certificates.len(),
 9042:         report.binary_size_bytes
 9043:     ))
 9044: }

 9181: /// Pure evaluator for the JSON output of `rustynetd
 9182: /// windows-mesh-status-check`. Returns a one-line success summary
 9183: /// when the daemon reports a current membership + assignment
 9184: /// snapshot, or a precise drift reason. Callable in tests without
 9185: /// SSH/IO.
 9186: fn evaluate_windows_mesh_join_report(
 9187:     windows_alias: &str,
 9188:     raw_json: &str,
 9189: ) -> Result<String, String> {
 9190:     let report: rustynetd::windows_mesh_status::WindowsMeshStatusReport =
 9191:         serde_json::from_str(raw_json)
 9192:             .map_err(|err| format!("parse windows-mesh-status-check JSON output failed: {err}"))?;
 9193:     if report.schema_version != 1 {
 9194:         return Err(format!(
 9195:             "windows-mesh-status-check returned unsupported schema_version={}",
 9196:             report.schema_version
 9197:         ));
 9198:     }
 9199:     if !report.overall_ok {
 9200:         let reasons = if report.drift_reasons.is_empty() {
 9201:             "report set overall_ok=false but no drift_reasons recorded; output is inconsistent"
 9202:                 .to_string()
 9203:         } else {
 9204:             report.drift_reasons.join("; ")
 9205:         };
 9206:         return Err(format!("Windows mesh-join state drift detected: {reasons}"));
 9207:     }
 9208:     if !report.drift_reasons.is_empty() {
 9209:         return Err(format!(
 9210:             "report set overall_ok=true but drift_reasons is non-empty: {}",
 9211:             report.drift_reasons.join("; ")
 9212:         ));
 9213:     }
 9214:     let summary_detail = match &report.snapshot {
 9215:         rustynetd::windows_mesh_status::WindowsMeshSnapshotLoad::Ok {
 9216:             peer_ids,
 9217:             age_seconds,
 9218:             ..
 9219:         } => format!("peers={} age_seconds={}", peer_ids.len(), age_seconds),
 9220:         // The variants below would normally be drift cases handled
 9221:         // above (overall_ok=false). They appear here only on a
 9222:         // self-inconsistent payload — keep the summary informative
 9223:         // rather than panicking.
 9224:         rustynetd::windows_mesh_status::WindowsMeshSnapshotLoad::Missing { reason } => {
 9225:             format!("inconsistent: load_status=missing reason={reason}")
 9226:         }
 9227:         rustynetd::windows_mesh_status::WindowsMeshSnapshotLoad::IntegrityMismatch { reason } => {
 9228:             format!("inconsistent: load_status=integrity-mismatch reason={reason}")
 9229:         }
 9230:         rustynetd::windows_mesh_status::WindowsMeshSnapshotLoad::InvalidFormat { reason } => {
 9231:             format!("inconsistent: load_status=invalid-format reason={reason}")
 9232:         }
 9233:     };
 9234:     Ok(format!(
 9235:         "Windows mesh-join state verified on {windows_alias} ({summary_detail})"
 9236:     ))
 9237: }

 9239: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 9240: // W4.2-followup: Windows membership-snapshot distribution
 9241: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 9242: 
 9243: /// Reviewed Windows-side bundle distribution contract — the path
 9244: /// triple every signed bundle's distribution helper needs (canonical
 9245: /// landing path, watermark path the daemon's WatermarkStore reads,
 9246: /// staging directory for in-flight uploads, filename prefix for the
 9247: /// per-run unique staging file).
 9248: ///
 9249: /// All four bundle types — membership, assignment, traversal,
 9250: /// dns-zone — share the same scp + atomic-install + watermark-clear
 9251: /// pattern, distinguished only by the constants in the contract.
 9252: /// Funnelling them through a single dispatch fn means there is one
 9253: /// audited code path for every bundle distribution rather than four
 9254: /// near-duplicates.
 9255: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
 9256: struct WindowsBundleDistributionContract {
 9257:     /// Human-readable label included in the success summary, error
 9258:     /// messages, and the staging-filename charset rejection. Keep
 9259:     /// it lowercase + hyphens so log lines stay grep-stable.
 9260:     label: &'static str,
 9261:     /// Canonical landing path on the Windows guest. The daemon's
 9262:     /// fetcher reads this on every refresh tick.
 9263:     canonical_path: &'static str,
 9264:     /// Watermark-store path the daemon's WatermarkStore reads.
 9265:     /// Deleting this file forces the daemon to re-ingest the new
 9266:     /// bundle on next refresh — same semantics as
 9267:     /// `root rm -f /var/lib/rustynet/<bundle>.watermark` on the
 9268:     /// Linux orchestrator's distribute_*_worker fns.
 9269:     watermark_path: &'static str,
 9270:     /// Staging directory for in-flight uploads. Atomic install
 9271:     /// pattern: upload to a per-run unique filename under
 9272:     /// `.staging\`, then `Move-Item -Force` over the canonical path.
 9273:     /// Lives under the same reviewed `C:\ProgramData\RustyNet\…`
 9274:     /// subtree as the canonical path so the upload transit window
 9275:     /// does not expose the bundle to a wider audience than its
 9276:     /// final ACL.
 9277:     staging_dir: &'static str,
 9278:     /// Prefix for the per-run unique staging filename. The full
 9279:     /// filename is `<prefix>.<hex-u128>.staging`. Fixed prefix +
 9280:     /// generated suffix is the only shape the install-script
 9281:     /// charset filter accepts.
 9282:     staging_prefix: &'static str,
 9283: }
 9284: 
 9285: const WINDOWS_BUNDLE_MEMBERSHIP: WindowsBundleDistributionContract =
 9286:     WindowsBundleDistributionContract {
 9287:         label: "membership",
 9288:         canonical_path: r"C:\ProgramData\RustyNet\membership\membership.snapshot",
 9289:         watermark_path: r"C:\ProgramData\RustyNet\membership\membership.watermark",
 9290:         staging_dir: r"C:\ProgramData\RustyNet\membership\.staging",
 9291:         staging_prefix: "membership.snapshot",
 9292:     };
 9293: 
 9294: const WINDOWS_BUNDLE_ASSIGNMENT: WindowsBundleDistributionContract =
 9295:     WindowsBundleDistributionContract {
 9296:         label: "assignment",
 9297:         canonical_path: r"C:\ProgramData\RustyNet\trust\rustynetd.assignment",
 9298:         watermark_path: r"C:\ProgramData\RustyNet\trust\rustynetd.assignment.watermark",
 9299:         staging_dir: r"C:\ProgramData\RustyNet\trust\.staging",
 9300:         staging_prefix: "rustynetd.assignment",
 9301:     };
 9302: 
 9303: const WINDOWS_BUNDLE_TRAVERSAL: WindowsBundleDistributionContract =
 9304:     WindowsBundleDistributionContract {
 9305:         label: "traversal",
 9306:         canonical_path: r"C:\ProgramData\RustyNet\trust\rustynetd.traversal",
 9307:         watermark_path: r"C:\ProgramData\RustyNet\trust\rustynetd.traversal.watermark",
 9308:         staging_dir: r"C:\ProgramData\RustyNet\trust\.staging",
 9309:         staging_prefix: "rustynetd.traversal",
 9310:     };
 9311: 
 9312: const WINDOWS_BUNDLE_DNS_ZONE: WindowsBundleDistributionContract =
 9313:     WindowsBundleDistributionContract {
 9314:         label: "dns-zone",
 9315:         canonical_path: r"C:\ProgramData\RustyNet\trust\rustynetd.dns-zone",
 9316:         watermark_path: r"C:\ProgramData\RustyNet\trust\rustynetd.dns-zone.watermark",
 9317:         staging_dir: r"C:\ProgramData\RustyNet\trust\.staging",
 9318:         staging_prefix: "rustynetd.dns-zone",
 9319:     };
 9320: 
 9321: // Verifier-key distribution contracts. The Windows daemon's
 9322: // auto-tunnel / traversal / DNS-zone bundle ingest paths each load a
 9323: // peer-set verifier key from a fixed canonical path
 9324: // (`crates/rustynetd/src/windows_paths.rs:31-44`). Without those keys
 9325: // the daemon's bundle preflight rejects every signed bundle as
 9326: // "verifier key not found" / "read verifier key failed", and the
 9327: // `validate_windows_mesh_join` stage fails with empty peer state.
 9328: //
 9329: // Each verifier-key contract reuses the bundle distribution
 9330: // machinery: SCP to staging, atomic Move-Item to canonical. The
 9331: // `watermark_path` field is set to a sentinel filename that never
 9332: // exists on disk; the install-script's watermark-clear step is
 9333: // already gated on `Test-Path`, so no Remove-Item ever fires for
 9334: // these contracts. Verifier keys are static config, not signed
 9335: // bundles with freshness watermarks.
 9336: const WINDOWS_BUNDLE_ASSIGNMENT_VERIFIER_KEY: WindowsBundleDistributionContract =
 9337:     WindowsBundleDistributionContract {
 9338:         label: "assignment-verifier-key",
 9339:         canonical_path: r"C:\ProgramData\RustyNet\trust\assignment.pub",
 9340:         watermark_path: r"C:\ProgramData\RustyNet\trust\assignment.pub.no-watermark-sentinel",
 9341:         staging_dir: r"C:\ProgramData\RustyNet\trust\.staging",
 9342:         staging_prefix: "assignment.pub",
 9343:     };
 9344: 
 9345: const WINDOWS_BUNDLE_TRAVERSAL_VERIFIER_KEY: WindowsBundleDistributionContract =
 9346:     WindowsBundleDistributionContract {
 9347:         label: "traversal-verifier-key",
 9348:         canonical_path: r"C:\ProgramData\RustyNet\trust\traversal.pub",
 9349:         watermark_path: r"C:\ProgramData\RustyNet\trust\traversal.pub.no-watermark-sentinel",
 9350:         staging_dir: r"C:\ProgramData\RustyNet\trust\.staging",
 9351:         staging_prefix: "traversal.pub",
 9352:     };
 9353: 
 9354: const WINDOWS_BUNDLE_DNS_ZONE_VERIFIER_KEY: WindowsBundleDistributionContract =
 9355:     WindowsBundleDistributionContract {
 9356:         label: "dns-zone-verifier-key",
 9357:         canonical_path: r"C:\ProgramData\RustyNet\trust\dns-zone.pub",
 9358:         watermark_path: r"C:\ProgramData\RustyNet\trust\dns-zone.pub.no-watermark-sentinel",
 9359:         staging_dir: r"C:\ProgramData\RustyNet\trust\.staging",
 9360:         staging_prefix: "dns-zone.pub",
 9361:     };

 9363: /// Build the PowerShell script body that ensures the staging
 9364: /// directory exists. `New-Item -Force` is idempotent. The path is
 9365: /// a hard-coded reviewed constant so no untrusted value crosses the
 9366: /// PowerShell boundary; we still wrap through `powershell_quote`
 9367: /// for argv-only consistency with the rest of the orchestrator's
 9368: /// PS construction.
 9369: #[allow(dead_code)]
 9370: fn build_windows_bundle_ensure_staging_dir_script(
 9371:     contract: &WindowsBundleDistributionContract,
 9372: ) -> Result<String, String> {
 9373:     let quoted_dir = powershell_quote(contract.staging_dir)?;
 9374:     Ok(format!(
 9375:         "New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path {quoted_dir} | Out-Null"
 9376:     ))
 9377: }
 9378: 
 9379: /// Build the atomic install + watermark-clear PowerShell body. The
 9380: /// staging filename is filtered to ASCII alphanumeric + `-` `_` `.`
 9381: /// only — defense-in-depth against a future caller who feeds an
 9382: /// operator-controlled value into the staging-name parameter and
 9383: /// inadvertently lets `\`-traversal or PS literal escapes through.
 9384: #[allow(dead_code)]
 9385: fn build_windows_bundle_atomic_install_script(
 9386:     contract: &WindowsBundleDistributionContract,
 9387:     staging_filename: &str,
 9388: ) -> Result<String, String> {
 9389:     let label_field = format!("windows {} staging filename", contract.label);
 9390:     ensure_no_control_chars(label_field.as_str(), staging_filename)?;
 9391:     if staging_filename.is_empty() {
 9392:         return Err(format!(
 9393:             "windows {} staging filename must not be empty",
 9394:             contract.label
 9395:         ));
 9396:     }
 9397:     for ch in staging_filename.chars() {
 9398:         if !(ch.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || ch == '-' || ch == '_' || ch == '.') {
 9399:             return Err(format!(
 9400:                 "windows {} staging filename rejected on {ch:?}; allowed: ASCII alphanumeric + '-' '_' '.'",
 9401:                 contract.label
 9402:             ));
 9403:         }
 9404:     }
 9405:     let staging_full = format!("{}\\{}", contract.staging_dir, staging_filename);
 9406:     let quoted_staging = powershell_quote(&staging_full)?;
 9407:     let quoted_canonical = powershell_quote(contract.canonical_path)?;
 9408:     let quoted_watermark = powershell_quote(contract.watermark_path)?;
 9409:     // `Remove-Item -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` against a non-existent path
 9410:     // silences the error stream but still propagates a non-zero exit through
 9411:     // the SSH `powershell.exe -Command` host, which the orchestrator reads as
 9412:     // a stage failure even though the move + watermark-clear semantics are
 9413:     // correct. Gate the watermark removal on Test-Path and end with an
 9414:     // explicit `exit 0` so the only paths to a non-zero exit are: (1)
 9415:     // Move-Item raising a terminating error, or (2) Remove-Item failing on
 9416:     // a watermark that genuinely exists.
 9417:     Ok(format!(
 9418:         "Move-Item -Force -LiteralPath {quoted_staging} -Destination {quoted_canonical}; \
 9419:          if (Test-Path -LiteralPath {quoted_watermark}) {{ Remove-Item -Force -LiteralPath {quoted_watermark} }}; \
 9420:          exit 0"
 9421:     ))
 9422: }
 9423: 
 9424: /// Per-run unique staging filename. Format: `<prefix>.<hex-u128>.staging`.
 9425: #[allow(dead_code)]
 9426: fn windows_bundle_staging_filename(
 9427:     contract: &WindowsBundleDistributionContract,
 9428:     suffix: u128,
 9429: ) -> String {
 9430:     format!("{}.{suffix:032x}.staging", contract.staging_prefix)
 9431: }
 9432: 
 9433: /// Single audited dispatch fn for every Windows-side signed-bundle
 9434: /// distribution. Three SSH/SCP round-trips per the plan §6.4
 9435: /// contract: ensure staging dir, scp to staging, atomic install +
 9436: /// watermark clear.
 9437: ///
 9438: /// Today the Windows daemon ships on `windows-unsupported` and
 9439: /// refuses to start, so a pushed bundle will not be ingested until
 9440: /// a working backend lands (tracked in
 9441: /// `WindowsWorkingNodePlan_2026-04-17.md`). The distribution code
 9442: /// path is correct + ready; the file lands in the daemon-expected
 9443: /// location with the daemon-expected ACL inherited from the W1.1
 9444: /// reviewed parent root.
 9445: #[allow(dead_code)]
 9446: fn run_distribute_windows_bundle_stage(
 9447:     contract: &WindowsBundleDistributionContract,
 9448:     windows_alias: &str,
 9449:     inventory_path: &Path,
 9450:     ssh_identity_file: &Path,
 9451:     known_hosts_path: Option<&Path>,
 9452:     local_bundle_path: &Path,
 9453: ) -> Result<(String, String), (String, String)> {
 9454:     if !local_bundle_path.is_file() {
 9455:         return Err((
 9456:             format!(
 9457:                 "local {} bundle not a regular file: {}",
 9458:                 contract.label,
 9459:                 local_bundle_path.display()
 9460:             ),
 9461:             String::new(),
 9462:         ));
 9463:     }
 9464: 
 9465:     let targets = resolve_remote_targets(inventory_path, &[windows_alias.to_string()], false, &[])
 9466:         .map_err(|err| (err, String::new()))?;
 9467:     let target = targets.into_iter().next().ok_or_else(|| {
 9468:         (
 9469:             format!("no target resolved for alias {windows_alias}"),
 9470:             String::new(),
 9471:         )
 9472:     })?;
 9473:     if target.platform_profile.platform != VmGuestPlatform::Windows {
 9474:         return Err((
 9475:             format!(
 9476:                 "alias {windows_alias} resolved to non-Windows platform: {}",
 9477:                 target.platform_profile.platform.as_str()
 9478:             ),
 9479:             String::new(),
 9480:         ));
 9481:     }
 9482: 
 9483:     let timeout = timeout_or_default(0, DEFAULT_RUN_TIMEOUT_SECS);
 9484: 
 9485:     // Step 1: ensure staging dir exists.
 9486:     let ensure_dir_script = build_windows_bundle_ensure_staging_dir_script(contract)
 9487:         .map_err(|err| (err, String::new()))?;
 9488:     let ensure_dir_invocation = build_ssh_powershell_encoded_invocation(ensure_dir_script.as_str())
 9489:         .map_err(|err| (err, String::new()))?;
 9490:     let _ = capture_remote_shell_command_for_target(
 9491:         &target,
 9492:         None,
 9493:         Some(ssh_identity_file),
 9494:         known_hosts_path,
 9495:         ensure_dir_invocation.as_str(),
 9496:         timeout,
 9497:     )
 9498:     .map_err(|err| {
 9499:         (
 9500:             format!(
 9501:                 "ensure-staging-dir for windows {} distribution failed: {err}",
 9502:                 contract.label
 9503:             ),
 9504:             String::new(),
 9505:         )
 9506:     })?;
 9507: 
 9508:     // Step 2: SCP local bundle to staging.
 9509:     let staging_filename = windows_bundle_staging_filename(contract, unique_suffix());
 9510:     let staging_remote_path = format!("{}\\{}", contract.staging_dir, staging_filename);
 9511:     let scp_status = scp_to_remote_for_target(
 9512:         &target,
 9513:         None,
 9514:         Some(ssh_identity_file),
 9515:         known_hosts_path,
 9516:         local_bundle_path,
 9517:         staging_remote_path.as_str(),
 9518:         timeout,
 9519:     )
 9520:     .map_err(|err| {
 9521:         (
 9522:             format!(
 9523:                 "scp of windows {} bundle to staging failed: {err}",
 9524:                 contract.label
 9525:             ),
 9526:             String::new(),
 9527:         )
 9528:     })?;
 9529:     if !scp_status.success() {
 9530:         return Err((
 9531:             format!(
 9532:                 "scp of windows {} bundle to staging exited non-zero: {}",
 9533:                 contract.label,
 9534:                 status_code(scp_status)
 9535:             ),
 9536:             String::new(),
 9537:         ));
 9538:     }
 9539: 
 9540:     // Step 3: atomic install + delete watermark.
 9541:     let install_script =
 9542:         build_windows_bundle_atomic_install_script(contract, staging_filename.as_str())
 9543:             .map_err(|err| (err, String::new()))?;
 9544:     let install_invocation = build_ssh_powershell_encoded_invocation(install_script.as_str())
 9545:         .map_err(|err| (err, String::new()))?;
 9546:     let _ = capture_remote_shell_command_for_target(
 9547:         &target,
 9548:         None,
 9549:         Some(ssh_identity_file),
 9550:         known_hosts_path,
 9551:         install_invocation.as_str(),
 9552:         timeout,
 9553:     )
 9554:     .map_err(|err| {
 9555:         (
 9556:             format!(
 9557:                 "atomic install of windows {} bundle failed: {err}",
 9558:                 contract.label
 9559:             ),
 9560:             String::new(),
 9561:         )
 9562:     })?;
 9563: 
 9564:     Ok((
 9565:         format!(
 9566:             "Windows {} bundle distributed to {windows_alias} (staging={staging_filename}, canonical={})",
 9567:             contract.label, contract.canonical_path
 9568:         ),
 9569:         String::new(),
 9570:     ))
 9571: }

 9723: // =====================================================================
 9724: // Windows membership/assignment helpers (W4.2 live-mesh prep)
 9725: //
 9726: // These functions implement the two orchestration stages that prepare
 9727: // the Windows node to join the mesh: amending the Linux membership to
 9728: // include the Windows node, and issuing a Windows-specific signed
 9729: // assignment bundle. Both helpers are called only when `linux_exit_alias`
 9730: // is populated in `WindowsOrchestrationOptions`.
 9731: // =====================================================================
 9732: 
 9733: /// Validates that `id` is safe for use as a node-id in CLI flags and spec
 9734: /// strings: ASCII alphanumeric + hyphen + underscore, 1-63 chars.
 9735: fn validate_mesh_node_id(id: &str) -> Result<(), String> {
 9736:     if id.is_empty() || id.len() > 63 {
 9737:         return Err(format!("node ID must be 1-63 characters: {id:?}"));
 9738:     }
 9739:     if !id
 9740:         .chars()
 9741:         .all(|c| c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || c == '-' || c == '_')
 9742:     {
 9743:         return Err(format!(
 9744:             "node ID must be ASCII alphanumeric + hyphen + underscore: {id:?}"
 9745:         ));
 9746:     }
 9747:     Ok(())
 9748: }
 9749: 
 9750: /// Validates that `addr` is safe for use as an endpoint address in NODES_SPEC:
 9751: /// ASCII alphanumeric + dot + colon + hyphen, rejecting the `|` and `;`
 9752: /// separators used in the spec format.
 9753: fn validate_mesh_endpoint_address(addr: &str) -> Result<(), String> {
 9754:     if addr.is_empty() {
 9755:         return Err("endpoint address must not be empty".to_string());
 9756:     }
 9757:     if !addr
 9758:         .chars()
 9759:         .all(|c| c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || c == '.' || c == ':' || c == '-')
 9760:     {
 9761:         return Err(format!(
 9762:             "endpoint address contains invalid characters: {addr:?}"
 9763:         ));
 9764:     }
 9765:     Ok(())
 9766: }
 9767: 
 9768: /// Extracts the unquoted value of `key` from a simple `KEY="value"` env file
 9769: /// body. Returns `None` when the key is absent. Delegates to `parse_env_value`
 9770: /// so it handles the same escape sequences as `format_env_assignment`.
 9771: fn extract_env_var_from_text(text: &str, key: &str) -> Option<String> {
 9772:     for line in text.lines() {
 9773:         let trimmed = line.trim();
 9774:         if trimmed.is_empty() || trimmed.starts_with('#') {
 9775:             continue;
 9776:         }
 9777:         if let Some((k, raw_value)) = trimmed.split_once('=')
 9778:             && k == key
 9779:         {
 9780:             return parse_env_value(raw_value).ok();
 9781:         }
 9782:     }
 9783:     None
 9784: }
 9785: 
 9786: /// Adds `windows_alias` to the Linux mesh membership on `exit_alias` and
 9787: /// fetches the updated `membership.snapshot`.
 9788: ///
 9789: /// Collects the Windows WireGuard pubkey via PowerShell, runs
 9790: /// `rustynet ops e2e-membership-add` on the exit node, then captures the
 9791: /// updated snapshot to `<report_dir>/state/windows-membership.snapshot`.
 9792: ///
 9793: /// On success sets `*out_wg_pubkey_hex` (64-char hex) and
 9794: /// `*out_membership_path` (local snapshot path).
 9795: #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
 9796: fn amend_membership_for_windows_node(
 9797:     windows_alias: &str,
 9798:     exit_alias: &str,
 9799:     inventory_path: &Path,
 9800:     ssh_identity_file: &Path,
 9801:     known_hosts_path: Option<&Path>,
 9802:     report_dir: &Path,
 9803:     out_wg_pubkey_hex: &mut Option<String>,
 9804:     out_membership_path: &mut Option<PathBuf>,
 9805: ) -> Result<String, String> {
 9806:     let inventory = load_inventory(inventory_path)?;
 9807:     let windows_entry = inventory
 9808:         .iter()
 9809:         .find(|e| e.alias == windows_alias)
 9810:         .ok_or_else(|| format!("Windows alias {windows_alias:?} not found in inventory"))?
 9811:         .clone();
 9812:     let windows_node_id = windows_entry
 9813:         .node_id
 9814:         .as_deref()
 9815:         .ok_or_else(|| format!("inventory entry for {windows_alias:?} has no node_id"))?;
 9816:     validate_mesh_node_id(windows_node_id)?;
 9817:     let windows_target = remote_target_from_inventory_entry(&windows_entry, None);
 9818:     let exit_entry = inventory
 9819:         .iter()
 9820:         .find(|e| e.alias == exit_alias)
 9821:         .ok_or_else(|| format!("exit alias {exit_alias:?} not found in inventory"))?
 9822:         .clone();
 9823:     let exit_node_id = exit_entry
 9824:         .node_id
 9825:         .as_deref()
 9826:         .ok_or_else(|| format!("inventory entry for {exit_alias:?} has no node_id"))?;
 9827:     let exit_target = remote_target_from_inventory_entry(&exit_entry, None);
 9828: 
 9829:     // Collect the Windows WireGuard public key (base64 on disk → hex).
 9830:     // The key file is written by the daemon at startup.
 9831:     let wg_pub_ps = concat!(
 9832:         "$b=[Convert]::FromBase64String(",
 9833:         "(Get-Content -LiteralPath 'C:\\ProgramData\\RustyNet\\keys\\wireguard.pub' -Raw).Trim());",
 9834:         " -join($b|%{$_.ToString('x2')})"
 9835:     );
 9836:     let raw_hex = capture_remote_shell_command_for_target(
 9837:         &windows_target,
 9838:         None,
 9839:         Some(ssh_identity_file),
 9840:         known_hosts_path,
 9841:         wg_pub_ps,
 9842:         Duration::from_secs(30),
 9843:     )
 9844:     .map_err(|e| format!("collect Windows WireGuard pubkey from {windows_alias} failed: {e}"))?;
 9845:     let pubkey_hex = raw_hex.trim().to_string();
 9846:     if pubkey_hex.len() != 64 || !pubkey_hex.chars().all(|c| c.is_ascii_hexdigit()) {
 9847:         return Err(format!(
 9848:             "Windows WireGuard pubkey from {windows_alias} is not a 64-char lowercase hex \
 9849:              string: {pubkey_hex:?}"
 9850:         ));
 9851:     }
 9852: 
 9853:     // Add the Windows node to the Linux membership on the exit node.
 9854:     let owner_approver_id = format!("{exit_node_id}-owner");
 9855:     let add_script = format!(
 9856:         "set -eu; sudo -n rustynet ops e2e-membership-add \
 9857:          --client-node-id {node_id} \
 9858:          --client-pubkey-hex {pubkey} \
 9859:          --owner-approver-id {approver}",
 9860:         node_id = shell_quote(windows_node_id),
 9861:         pubkey = shell_quote(pubkey_hex.as_str()),
 9862:         approver = shell_quote(owner_approver_id.as_str()),
 9863:     );
 9864:     let add_out = capture_remote_shell_command_for_target(
 9865:         &exit_target,
 9866:         None,
 9867:         Some(ssh_identity_file),
 9868:         known_hosts_path,
 9869:         add_script.as_str(),
 9870:         Duration::from_secs(60),
 9871:     )
 9872:     .map_err(|e| format!("e2e-membership-add on {exit_alias} failed: {e}"))?;
 9873: 
 9874:     // Fetch the updated membership snapshot from the exit node.
 9875:     let snapshot_path = report_dir.join("state").join("windows-membership.snapshot");
 9876:     capture_remote_file_to_local(
 9877:         &exit_target,
 9878:         None,
 9879:         Some(ssh_identity_file),
 9880:         known_hosts_path,
 9881:         "/var/lib/rustynet/membership.snapshot",
 9882:         snapshot_path.as_path(),
 9883:         Duration::from_secs(30),
 9884:     )
 9885:     .map_err(|e| format!("fetch membership.snapshot from {exit_alias} failed: {e}"))?;
 9886: 
 9887:     *out_wg_pubkey_hex = Some(pubkey_hex.clone());
 9888:     *out_membership_path = Some(snapshot_path.clone());
 9889: 
 9890:     Ok(format!(
 9891:         "amended Linux membership to include {windows_alias} ({windows_node_id}) on \
 9892:          {exit_alias}: pubkey={pubkey_hex} add_output={} snapshot={}",
 9893:         add_out.trim(),
 9894:         snapshot_path.display(),
 9895:     ))
 9896: }
 9897: 
 9898: /// Issues a signed assignment bundle for the Windows node.
 9899: ///
 9900: /// Reads the existing Linux assignment env (`<report_dir>/state/issue_assignments.env`),
 9901: /// appends the Windows node to `NODES_SPEC` and `ALLOW_SPEC`, sets
 9902: /// `ASSIGNMENTS_SPEC` to only the Windows node (the Linux peers' bundles are
 9903: /// unchanged), SCPs the extended env to the exit node, runs
 9904: /// `e2e-issue-assignment-bundles-from-env`, and fetches the produced bundle.
 9905: ///
 9906: /// On success sets `*out_assignment_path` to the local bundle path.
 9907: #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
 9908: fn issue_assignment_for_windows_node(
 9909:     windows_alias: &str,
 9910:     exit_alias: &str,
 9911:     windows_wg_pubkey_hex: &str,
 9912:     inventory_path: &Path,
 9913:     ssh_identity_file: &Path,
 9914:     known_hosts_path: Option<&Path>,
 9915:     report_dir: &Path,
 9916:     out_assignment_path: &mut Option<PathBuf>,
 9917: ) -> Result<String, String> {
 9918:     let inventory = load_inventory(inventory_path)?;
 9919:     let windows_entry = inventory
 9920:         .iter()
 9921:         .find(|e| e.alias == windows_alias)
 9922:         .ok_or_else(|| format!("Windows alias {windows_alias:?} not found in inventory"))?
 9923:         .clone();
 9924:     let windows_node_id = windows_entry
 9925:         .node_id
 9926:         .as_deref()
 9927:         .ok_or_else(|| format!("inventory entry for {windows_alias:?} has no node_id"))?;
 9928:     validate_mesh_node_id(windows_node_id)?;
 9929:     let windows_ip = windows_entry
 9930:         .last_known_ip
 9931:         .as_deref()
 9932:         .ok_or_else(|| format!("inventory entry for {windows_alias:?} has no last_known_ip"))?;
 9933:     validate_mesh_endpoint_address(windows_ip)?;
 9934:     let exit_entry = inventory
 9935:         .iter()
 9936:         .find(|e| e.alias == exit_alias)
 9937:         .ok_or_else(|| format!("exit alias {exit_alias:?} not found in inventory"))?
 9938:         .clone();
 9939:     let exit_node_id = exit_entry
 9940:         .node_id
 9941:         .as_deref()
 9942:         .ok_or_else(|| format!("inventory entry for {exit_alias:?} has no node_id"))?;
 9943:     let exit_target = remote_target_from_inventory_entry(&exit_entry, None);
 9944: 
 9945:     // Read and parse the base assignment env produced by the Linux bash orchestrator.
 9946:     let base_env_path = report_dir.join("state").join("issue_assignments.env");
 9947:     if !base_env_path.is_file() {
 9948:         return Err(format!(
 9949:             "base assignment env not found at {}; run Linux issue stages first",
 9950:             base_env_path.display()
 9951:         ));
 9952:     }
 9953:     let env_text = std::fs::read_to_string(&base_env_path)
 9954:         .map_err(|e| format!("read base assignment env failed: {e}"))?;
 9955:     let nodes_spec = extract_env_var_from_text(env_text.as_str(), "NODES_SPEC")
 9956:         .ok_or_else(|| "NODES_SPEC not found in base assignment env".to_string())?;
 9957:     let allow_spec = extract_env_var_from_text(env_text.as_str(), "ALLOW_SPEC")
 9958:         .ok_or_else(|| "ALLOW_SPEC not found in base assignment env".to_string())?;
 9959: 
 9960:     // Extend the specs with the Windows node.
 9961:     // Port 51820 matches the hardcoded WireGuard listen port used by
 9962:     // `build_onehop_specs` in the Linux bash orchestrator.
 9963:     let windows_node_spec = format!("{windows_node_id}|{windows_ip}:51820|{windows_wg_pubkey_hex}");
 9964:     let extended_nodes_spec = format!("{nodes_spec};{windows_node_spec}");
 9965:     let extended_allow_spec =
 9966:         format!("{allow_spec};{windows_node_id}|{exit_node_id};{exit_node_id}|{windows_node_id}");
 9967:     let windows_assignments_spec = format!("{windows_node_id}|{exit_node_id}");
 9968: 
 9969:     // Write the extended env to a local temp file.
 9970:     let windows_env_path = report_dir
 9971:         .join("state")
 9972:         .join("issue_windows_assignment.env");
 9973:     let env_body = [
 9974:         format_env_assignment("NODES_SPEC", extended_nodes_spec.as_str())
 9975:             .map_err(|e| format!("format NODES_SPEC failed: {e}"))?,
 9976:         format_env_assignment("ALLOW_SPEC", extended_allow_spec.as_str())
 9977:             .map_err(|e| format!("format ALLOW_SPEC failed: {e}"))?,
 9978:         format_env_assignment("ASSIGNMENTS_SPEC", windows_assignments_spec.as_str())
 9979:             .map_err(|e| format!("format ASSIGNMENTS_SPEC failed: {e}"))?,
 9980:     ]
 9981:     .join("\n");
 9982:     std::fs::write(windows_env_path.as_path(), env_body.as_str())
 9983:         .map_err(|e| format!("write Windows assignment env failed: {e}"))?;
 9984: 
 9985:     // SCP env to exit, issue bundle, cleanup.
 9986:     let remote_env = format!("/tmp/rn-windows-assignment-{}.env", unique_suffix());
 9987:     ensure_success_status(
 9988:         scp_to_remote_for_target(
 9989:             &exit_target,
 9990:             None,
 9991:             Some(ssh_identity_file),
 9992:             known_hosts_path,
 9993:             windows_env_path.as_path(),
 9994:             remote_env.as_str(),
 9995:             Duration::from_secs(30),
 9996:         )
 9997:         .map_err(|e| format!("SCP Windows assignment env to {exit_alias} failed: {e}"))?,
 9998:         "SCP Windows assignment env to exit",
 9999:     )?;
10000:     let issue_script = format!(
10001:         "set -eu; \
10002:          sudo -n mkdir -p /run/rustynet/assignment-issue; \
10003:          sudo -n rustynet ops e2e-issue-assignment-bundles-from-env \
10004:            --env-file {remote_env}; \
10005:          sudo -n rm -f {remote_env}",
10006:         remote_env = shell_quote(remote_env.as_str()),
10007:     );
10008:     capture_remote_shell_command_for_target(
10009:         &exit_target,
10010:         None,
10011:         Some(ssh_identity_file),
10012:         known_hosts_path,
10013:         issue_script.as_str(),
10014:         Duration::from_secs(60),
10015:     )
10016:     .map_err(|e| format!("issue Windows assignment bundle on {exit_alias} failed: {e}"))?;
10017: 
10018:     // Fetch the issued bundle.
10019:     let remote_bundle_path =
10020:         format!("/run/rustynet/assignment-issue/rn-assignment-{windows_node_id}.assignment");
10021:     let local_bundle_path = report_dir
10022:         .join("state")
10023:         .join(format!("assignment-{windows_node_id}.bundle"));
10024:     capture_remote_file_to_local(
10025:         &exit_target,
10026:         None,
10027:         Some(ssh_identity_file),
10028:         known_hosts_path,
10029:         remote_bundle_path.as_str(),
10030:         local_bundle_path.as_path(),
10031:         Duration::from_secs(30),
10032:     )
10033:     .map_err(|e| format!("fetch Windows assignment bundle from {exit_alias} failed: {e}"))?;
10034: 
10035:     *out_assignment_path = Some(local_bundle_path.clone());
10036: 
10037:     Ok(format!(
10038:         "issued assignment bundle for {windows_alias} ({windows_node_id}) via {exit_alias}; \
10039:          bundle={}",
10040:         local_bundle_path.display(),
10041:     ))
10042: }
10043: 
10044: // =====================================================================
10045: // Linux daemon-side validator orchestration (W3.2-followup-7)
10046: //
10047: // Mirror of the Windows orchestrator's per-op stage runners + chainer
10048: // (see `run_validate_windows_*_stage` + `run_windows_orchestration_stages_with_options`).
10049: // Dispatches each `linux-*-check` subcommand of the live Linux peer's
10050: // installed `rustynetd` binary over SSH, parses the typed JSON report,
10051: // and emits Pass / Fail / Skipped outcomes the orchestrator's
10052: // `vm-lab-validate-linux-security` subcommand records into a typed
10053: // JSON summary.
10054: //
10055: // Linux peers are bootstrapped by the existing bash orchestrator
10056: // (`scripts/e2e/live_linux_lab_orchestrator.sh`); this stage set is
10057: // the *validator* path only — no install / access bootstrap stages
10058: // here. The orchestrator's heterogeneous live-lab can drive both
10059: // peer types through one trait surface (LinuxBashOrchestrator runs
10060: // the install path; this validator chainer probes the live state
10061: // after install).
10062: // =====================================================================
10063: 
10064: /// Canonical install path of `rustynetd` on Linux peers, mirroring
10065: /// `ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/rustynetd …` in
10066: /// `scripts/systemd/rustynetd.service`. Pinned in source so a future
10067: /// rename of the install path fails the
10068: /// `linux_daemon_check_invocation_pins_canonical_install_path` test
10069: /// rather than silently dispatching against a stale path.
10070: pub const LINUX_RUSTYNETD_PATH: &str = "/usr/local/bin/rustynetd";
10071: 
10072: /// Build the POSIX-shell invocation that calls one of the `linux-*-check`
10073: /// subcommands on the live Linux peer. Centralizes argv-only discipline
10074: /// so every stage helper goes through the same audited path: the
10075: /// daemon path + subcommand both flow through `shell_quote`, and the
10076: /// subcommand charset is filtered to ASCII alphanumeric + `-` (rejecting
10077: /// anything that could carry shell metacharacters).
10078: ///
10079: /// `extra_args` are appended after `--no-fail-on-drift`. Each extra arg
10080: /// flows through `shell_quote` and rejects control characters so a
10081: /// future caller cannot inject shell metacharacters via the override
10082: /// parameter. Used today for the mesh-status stage's
10083: /// `--state-path / --expected-peer-id / --max-age-seconds` overrides.
10084: fn build_linux_daemon_check_invocation(
10085:     daemon_path: &str,
10086:     subcommand: &str,
10087:     extra_args: &[String],
10088: ) -> Result<String, String> {
10089:     ensure_no_control_chars("linux daemon path", daemon_path)?;
10090:     ensure_no_control_chars("linux daemon subcommand", subcommand)?;
10091:     if subcommand.is_empty() {
10092:         return Err("linux daemon subcommand must not be empty".to_string());
10093:     }
10094:     if !subcommand
10095:         .chars()
10096:         .all(|c| c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || c == '-')
10097:     {
10098:         return Err(format!(
10099:             "linux daemon subcommand rejected on charset: {subcommand:?}; allowed: ASCII alphanumeric + '-'"
10100:         ));
10101:     }
10102:     let mut command = format!(
10103:         "{} {} --no-fail-on-drift",
10104:         shell_quote(daemon_path),
10105:         shell_quote(subcommand)
10106:     );
10107:     for arg in extra_args {
10108:         ensure_no_control_chars("linux daemon extra arg", arg.as_str())?;
10109:         command.push(' ');
10110:         command.push_str(shell_quote(arg.as_str()).as_str());
10111:     }
10112:     Ok(command)
10113: }
10114: 
10115: /// Generic SSH dispatcher for a Linux daemon-check subcommand. Resolves
10116: /// the alias, asserts the platform is Linux, builds the POSIX
10117: /// invocation, and returns the trimmed raw stdout. Stage runners parse
10118: /// that output through their op-specific evaluator.
10119: fn run_linux_daemon_check_remote(
10120:     linux_alias: &str,
10121:     inventory_path: &Path,
10122:     ssh_identity_file: &Path,
10123:     known_hosts_path: Option<&Path>,
10124:     subcommand: &str,
10125:     extra_args: &[String],
10126: ) -> Result<String, String> {
10127:     let targets = resolve_remote_targets(inventory_path, &[linux_alias.to_string()], false, &[])?;
10128:     let target = targets
10129:         .into_iter()
10130:         .next()
10131:         .ok_or_else(|| format!("no target resolved for alias {linux_alias}"))?;
10132:     if target.platform_profile.platform != VmGuestPlatform::Linux {
10133:         return Err(format!(
10134:             "alias {linux_alias} resolved to non-Linux platform: {}",
10135:             target.platform_profile.platform.as_str()
10136:         ));
10137:     }
10138:     let timeout = timeout_or_default(0, DEFAULT_RUN_TIMEOUT_SECS);
10139:     let invocation =
10140:         build_linux_daemon_check_invocation(LINUX_RUSTYNETD_PATH, subcommand, extra_args)?;
10141:     let raw_output = capture_remote_shell_command_for_target(
10142:         &target,
10143:         None,
10144:         Some(ssh_identity_file),
10145:         known_hosts_path,
10146:         invocation.as_str(),
10147:         timeout,
10148:     )
10149:     .map_err(|err| format!("remote dispatch of {subcommand} failed: {err}"))?;
10150:     Ok(raw_output.trim().to_string())
10151: }
10152: 
10153: /// Pure evaluator for the JSON output of `rustynetd linux-runtime-acls-check`.
10154: fn evaluate_linux_runtime_acls_report(linux_alias: &str, raw_json: &str) -> Result<String, String> {
10155:     let report: rustynetd::linux_runtime_acls::LinuxRuntimeAclReport =
10156:         serde_json::from_str(raw_json)
10157:             .map_err(|err| format!("parse linux-runtime-acls-check JSON output failed: {err}"))?;
10158:     if report.schema_version != 1 {
10159:         return Err(format!(
10160:             "linux-runtime-acls-check returned unsupported schema_version={}",
10161:             report.schema_version
10162:         ));
10163:     }
10164:     if report.roots.is_empty() {
10165:         return Err(
10166:             "linux-runtime-acls-check returned an empty roots list; expected the canonical \
10167:              Linux runtime root set"
10168:                 .to_string(),
10169:         );
10170:     }
10171:     if !report.overall_ok {
10172:         let drifted = report
10173:             .roots
10174:             .iter()
10175:             .filter_map(|entry| match &entry.status {
10176:                 rustynetd::linux_runtime_acls::LinuxRuntimeAclRootStatus::Ok => None,
10177:                 rustynetd::linux_runtime_acls::LinuxRuntimeAclRootStatus::Missing { reason } => {
10178:                     Some(format!("{} missing: {reason}", entry.label))
10179:                 }
10180:                 rustynetd::linux_runtime_acls::LinuxRuntimeAclRootStatus::Drifted { reason } => {
10181:                     Some(format!("{} drifted: {reason}", entry.label))
10182:                 }
10183:             })
10184:             .collect::<Vec<_>>();
10185:         let summary = if drifted.is_empty() {
10186:             "report set overall_ok=false but every per-root entry is Ok; output is inconsistent"
10187:                 .to_string()
10188:         } else {
10189:             drifted.join("; ")
10190:         };
10191:         return Err(format!("Linux runtime ACL drift detected: {summary}"));
10192:     }
10193:     let inspected = report.roots.len();
10194:     Ok(format!(
10195:         "Linux runtime ACLs verified on {linux_alias}: {inspected} reviewed roots passed"
10196:     ))
10197: }
10198: 
10199: fn evaluate_linux_mesh_status_report(linux_alias: &str, raw_json: &str) -> Result<String, String> {
10200:     let report: rustynetd::linux_mesh_status::LinuxMeshStatusReport =
10201:         serde_json::from_str(raw_json)
10202:             .map_err(|err| format!("parse linux-mesh-status-check JSON output failed: {err}"))?;
10203:     if report.schema_version != 1 {
10204:         return Err(format!(
10205:             "linux-mesh-status-check returned unsupported schema_version={}",
10206:             report.schema_version
10207:         ));
10208:     }
10209:     if !report.overall_ok {
10210:         let summary = if report.drift_reasons.is_empty() {
10211:             "report set overall_ok=false but no drift_reasons were recorded; output is inconsistent"
10212:                 .to_string()
10213:         } else {
10214:             report.drift_reasons.join("; ")
10215:         };
10216:         return Err(format!("Linux mesh status drift detected: {summary}"));
10217:     }
10218:     Ok(format!(
10219:         "Linux mesh status verified on {linux_alias}: state at {}",
10220:         report.state_path
10221:     ))
10222: }

10256: fn evaluate_linux_authenticode_report(linux_alias: &str, raw_json: &str) -> Result<String, String> {
10257:     let report: rustynetd::linux_authenticode::LinuxAuthenticodeReport =
10258:         serde_json::from_str(raw_json)
10259:             .map_err(|err| format!("parse linux-authenticode-check JSON output failed: {err}"))?;
10260:     if report.schema_version != 1 {
10261:         return Err(format!(
10262:             "linux-authenticode-check returned unsupported schema_version={}",
10263:             report.schema_version
10264:         ));
10265:     }
10266:     // The Linux daemon's authenticode subcommand always emits
10267:     // `applicable: false, overall_ok: true` because Linux does not
10268:     // enforce runtime binary signatures. Pass-through with a clear
10269:     // summary so the orchestrator records the not-applicable verdict
10270:     // honestly rather than silently passing.
10271:     if report.applicable {
10272:         // Future-proofing: if a slice ever wires dpkg/rpm signature
10273:         // verification, the report would flip applicable=true and
10274:         // overall_ok would carry the verdict.
10275:         if !report.overall_ok {
10276:             return Err(format!(
10277:                 "Linux authenticode check failed: {}",
10278:                 report.reason
10279:             ));
10280:         }
10281:         Ok(format!(
10282:             "Linux authenticode verified on {linux_alias}: {}",
10283:             report.reason
10284:         ))
10285:     } else {
10286:         Ok(format!(
10287:             "Linux authenticode not applicable on {linux_alias} (runtime binary signature \
10288:              attestation is Windows-specific; Linux relies on dpkg/rpm install-time signature \
10289:              verification)"
10290:         ))
10291:     }
10292: }
10293: 
10294: fn evaluate_linux_service_hardening_report(
10295:     linux_alias: &str,
10296:     raw_json: &str,
10297: ) -> Result<String, String> {
10298:     let report: rustynetd::linux_service_hardening::LinuxServiceHardeningReport =
10299:         serde_json::from_str(raw_json).map_err(|err| {
10300:             format!("parse linux-service-hardening-check JSON output failed: {err}")
10301:         })?;
10302:     if report.schema_version != 1 {
10303:         return Err(format!(
10304:             "linux-service-hardening-check returned unsupported schema_version={}",
10305:             report.schema_version
10306:         ));
10307:     }
10308:     if !report.probed {
10309:         return Err(format!(
10310:             "Linux service hardening probe could not run: {}",
10311:             report
10312:                 .probe_reason
10313:                 .as_deref()
10314:                 .unwrap_or("(no reason recorded)")
10315:         ));
10316:     }
10317:     if !report.overall_ok {
10318:         let summary = if report.drift_reasons.is_empty() {
10319:             "report set overall_ok=false but no drift_reasons were recorded; output is inconsistent"
10320:                 .to_string()
10321:         } else {
10322:             report.drift_reasons.join("; ")
10323:         };
10324:         return Err(format!("Linux service hardening drift detected: {summary}"));
10325:     }
10326:     Ok(format!(
10327:         "Linux service hardening verified on {linux_alias}: {} reviewed directives matched",
10328:         report.observed.len()
10329:     ))
10330: }

10332: fn evaluate_linux_dns_failclosed_report(
10333:     linux_alias: &str,
10334:     raw_json: &str,
10335: ) -> Result<String, String> {
10336:     let report: rustynetd::linux_dns_failclosed::LinuxDnsFailclosedReport =
10337:         serde_json::from_str(raw_json)
10338:             .map_err(|err| format!("parse linux-dns-failclosed-check JSON output failed: {err}"))?;
10339:     if report.schema_version != 1 {
10340:         return Err(format!(
10341:             "linux-dns-failclosed-check returned unsupported schema_version={}",
10342:             report.schema_version
10343:         ));
10344:     }
10345:     if !report.overall_ok {
10346:         let summary = if report.drift_reasons.is_empty() {
10347:             "report set overall_ok=false but no drift_reasons were recorded; output is inconsistent"
10348:                 .to_string()
10349:         } else {
10350:             report.drift_reasons.join("; ")
10351:         };
10352:         return Err(format!("Linux DNS fail-closed drift detected: {summary}"));
10353:     }
10354:     Ok(format!(
10355:         "Linux DNS fail-closed verified on {linux_alias}: resolv.conf at {} loopback-only",
10356:         report.snapshot.resolv_conf_path
10357:     ))
10358: }
10359: 
10360: /// Per-stage thin runner. All six follow the same shape: dispatch the
10361: /// subcommand over SSH, parse the typed JSON via the op-specific
10362: /// evaluator, return `(summary, raw)` on success or `(reason, raw)` on
10363: /// failure. The wrapper keeps the orchestrator-side stage code
10364: /// compact + matches the Windows side's per-op runner shape exactly.
10365: fn run_validate_linux_runtime_acls_stage(
10366:     linux_alias: &str,
10367:     inventory_path: &Path,
10368:     ssh_identity_file: &Path,
10369:     known_hosts_path: Option<&Path>,
10370: ) -> Result<(String, String), (String, String)> {
10371:     let raw = run_linux_daemon_check_remote(
10372:         linux_alias,
10373:         inventory_path,
10374:         ssh_identity_file,
10375:         known_hosts_path,
10376:         "linux-runtime-acls-check",
10377:         &[],
10378:     )
10379:     .map_err(|err| (err, String::new()))?;
10380:     evaluate_linux_runtime_acls_report(linux_alias, raw.as_str())
10381:         .map(|summary| (summary, raw.clone()))
10382:         .map_err(|reason| (reason, raw))
10383: }

10385: /// Build the `--state-path / --expected-peer-id / --max-age-seconds`
10386: /// extras for the mesh-status subcommand from a `MeshStatusOverrides`
10387: /// struct. Centralizes the override-to-argv mapping so callers don't
10388: /// have to re-derive it.
10389: fn build_linux_mesh_status_extra_args(overrides: &MeshStatusOverrides) -> Vec<String> {
10390:     let mut extras: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
10391:     if let Some(path) = overrides.state_path.as_ref() {
10392:         extras.push("--state-path".to_string());
10393:         extras.push(path.display().to_string());
10394:     }
10395:     for peer in &overrides.expected_peer_ids {
10396:         extras.push("--expected-peer-id".to_string());
10397:         extras.push(peer.clone());
10398:     }
10399:     if let Some(secs) = overrides.max_age_seconds {
10400:         extras.push("--max-age-seconds".to_string());
10401:         extras.push(secs.to_string());
10402:     }
10403:     extras
10404: }

10406: fn run_validate_linux_mesh_status_stage_with_overrides(
10407:     linux_alias: &str,
10408:     inventory_path: &Path,
10409:     ssh_identity_file: &Path,
10410:     known_hosts_path: Option<&Path>,
10411:     overrides: &MeshStatusOverrides,
10412: ) -> Result<(String, String), (String, String)> {
10413:     let extras = build_linux_mesh_status_extra_args(overrides);
10414:     let raw = run_linux_daemon_check_remote(
10415:         linux_alias,
10416:         inventory_path,
10417:         ssh_identity_file,
10418:         known_hosts_path,
10419:         "linux-mesh-status-check",
10420:         extras.as_slice(),
10421:     )
10422:     .map_err(|err| (err, String::new()))?;
10423:     evaluate_linux_mesh_status_report(linux_alias, raw.as_str())
10424:         .map(|summary| (summary, raw.clone()))
10425:         .map_err(|reason| (reason, raw))
10426: }
