26839:     #[test]
26840:     fn build_windows_bundle_atomic_install_script_rejects_metacharacters() {
26841:         // Defensive: the staging filename must be ASCII alphanumeric
26842:         // + '-' '_' '.'. Anything else (especially `\` for path
26843:         // traversal, or `'` for PS literal escape) rejects so a
26844:         // future caller cannot inject through the staging-name
26845:         // parameter. Same charset applies to every bundle contract.
26846:         for bad in [
26847:             "evil\\..\\membership.snapshot",
26848:             "name'; Remove-Item C:\\ProgramData\\RustyNet -Recurse",
26849:             "name with spaces",
26850:             "name`whoami`",
26851:             "name$(rm)",
26852:             "name;Remove-Item",
26853:             "",
26854:         ] {
26855:             for contract in [
26856:                 &super::WINDOWS_BUNDLE_MEMBERSHIP,
26857:                 &super::WINDOWS_BUNDLE_ASSIGNMENT,
26858:                 &super::WINDOWS_BUNDLE_TRAVERSAL,
26859:                 &super::WINDOWS_BUNDLE_DNS_ZONE,
26860:             ] {
26861:                 let err = super::build_windows_bundle_atomic_install_script(contract, bad)
26862:                     .expect_err(&format!(
26863:                         "staging filename {bad:?} for {} must be rejected",
26864:                         contract.label
26865:                     ));
26866:                 if bad.is_empty() {
26867:                     assert!(err.contains("must not be empty"), "unexpected: {err}");
26868:                 } else {
26869:                     assert!(
26870:                         err.contains("rejected") || err.to_lowercase().contains("control"),
26871:                         "unexpected error for {bad:?} on {}: {err}",
26872:                         contract.label
26873:                     );
26874:                 }
26875:             }
26876:         }
26877:     }

27025:     fn linux_only_required_capabilities_constant_matches_legacy_gate_intent() {
27026:         // The legacy gate required Linux+POSIX+systemd+linux-bash and
27027:         // implicitly Linux kernel features. The capability constant
27028:         // surfacing this set must include all the same checks; if a
27029:         // future cleanup widens the constant, this test pins the
27030:         // intent so the change is visible in review.
27031:         let required: std::collections::HashSet<_> =
27032:             super::LIVE_LAB_LINUX_ONLY_REQUIRED_CAPABILITIES
27033:                 .iter()
27034:                 .copied()
27035:                 .collect();
27036:         for cap in [
27037:             super::LiveLabStageCapability::PosixShell,
27038:             super::LiveLabStageCapability::Systemd,
27039:             super::LiveLabStageCapability::LinuxBashGuestExec,
27040:             super::LiveLabStageCapability::NftablesFiltering,
27041:             super::LiveLabStageCapability::SystemdResolvedDns,
27042:         ] {
27043:             assert!(
27044:                 required.contains(&cap),
27045:                 "linux-only capability constant must include {:?}",
27046:                 cap
27047:             );
27048:         }
27049:     }

27112:     fn linux_bash_orchestrator_continue_from_setup_implies_skip_setup_pair() {
27113:         // continue_from_setup is the orchestrator's "I detected reusable
27114:         // setup state" signal; it must translate to the same
27115:         // --skip-setup --preserve-report-state pair the bash script
27116:         // expects, even when the user did not pass --skip-setup
27117:         // explicitly. Without this the orchestrator would re-run setup
27118:         // stages that already produced reviewed evidence.

27120:         let mut inputs = baseline_live_lab_run_inputs();
27121:         inputs.skip_setup = false;
27122:         inputs.continue_from_setup = true;
27123:         let args = collect_command_args(&orchestrator.build_command(&inputs));
27124:         assert!(args.contains(&"--skip-setup".to_string()));
27125:         assert!(args.contains(&"--preserve-report-state".to_string()));
27126:     }

27280:     fn unsupported_runtime_paths_default_getters_propagate_blocker() {
27281:         // The trait's per-role default getters are convenience wrappers
27282:         // around `path_for`; when the impl is `Unsupported`, every
27283:         // convenience getter must propagate the same blocker error so
27284:         // callers cannot accidentally bypass the stub by reaching for
27285:         // a typed getter instead of `path_for`.
27286:         let paths = super::UnsupportedRuntimePaths::macos();
27287:         for getter_result in [
27288:             paths.install_root(),
27289:             paths.state_root(),
27290:             paths.config_root(),
27291:             paths.logs_root(),
27292:             paths.trust_root(),
27293:             paths.membership_root(),
27294:             paths.keys_root(),
27295:             paths.secrets_root(),
27296:         ] {
27297:             let err = getter_result.expect_err("typed getter on macos stub must reject");
27298:             assert!(
27299:                 err.contains("not yet defined for platform 'macos'"),
27300:                 "stub getter must propagate blocker: {err}"
27301:             );
27302:         }
27303:     }

27318:         for (platform, expected_label) in [

27320:             (super::VmGuestPlatform::Ios, "ios"),
27321:             (super::VmGuestPlatform::Android, "android"),
27322:         ] {

27324:             assert_eq!(stub.platform_label(), expected_label);

27326:                 .config_root()
27327:                 .expect_err("stub platform config_root must reject");

27329:                 err.contains(expected_label),

27598:     #[test]
27599:     fn windows_remote_exec_doubles_apostrophes_inside_arg_values() {
27600:         // PS single-quoted literals require '' to represent a single
27601:         // quote. Adapter must double every apostrophe; otherwise a
27602:         // value like `O'Connor` would close the literal early and let
27603:         // the rest become PS code.
27604:         let exec = super::WindowsRemoteExec;
27605:         let inv = exec
27606:             .build_invocation(
27607:                 "windows@host",
27608:                 &["cmd.exe".to_string(), "O'Connor".to_string()],
27609:             )
27610:             .expect("must build");
27611:         match inv {
27612:             super::RemoteInvocation::WindowsSshEncodedPowerShell {
27613:                 powershell_body, ..
27614:             } => {
27615:                 assert!(
27616:                     powershell_body.contains("'O''Connor'"),
27617:                     "apostrophe must be doubled: {powershell_body}"
27618:                 );
27619:             }
27620:             _ => panic!("expected windows variant"),
27621:         }
27622:     }

27705:     #[test]
27706:     fn linux_daemon_probe_emits_argv_for_every_op() {
27707:         // The Linux daemon now ships every parity validator subcommand
27708:         // at the wire-format level. Each op resolves to its
27709:         // `linux-*-check` subcommand wired in
27710:         // `crates/rustynetd/src/main.rs`. The Linux + Windows probe
27711:         // surfaces are at full parity; the daemon-side enforcement
27712:         // posture differs only where the underlying mechanism does not
27713:         // exist on Linux (eg. authenticode emits applicable=false,
27714:         // overall_ok=true rather than rejecting).
27715:         let probe = super::LinuxDaemonProbe;
27716:         assert_eq!(probe.platform_label(), "linux");
27717:         for (op, expected_subcommand) in [
27718:             (
27719:                 super::DaemonProbeOp::RuntimeAcls,
27720:                 "linux-runtime-acls-check",
27721:             ),
27722:             (super::DaemonProbeOp::MeshStatus, "linux-mesh-status-check"),
27723:             (super::DaemonProbeOp::KeyCustody, "linux-key-custody-check"),
27724:             (
27725:                 super::DaemonProbeOp::Authenticode,
27726:                 "linux-authenticode-check",
27727:             ),
27728:             (
27729:                 super::DaemonProbeOp::ServiceHardening,
27730:                 "linux-service-hardening-check",
27731:             ),
27732:             (
27733:                 super::DaemonProbeOp::DnsFailclosed,
27734:                 "linux-dns-failclosed-check",
27735:             ),
27736:         ] {
27737:             let argv = probe
27738:                 .build_argv(op, std::path::Path::new("/usr/local/bin/rustynetd"))
27739:                 .expect("every op must resolve to a Linux subcommand at parity");
27740:             assert_eq!(
27741:                 argv,
27742:                 vec![
27743:                     "/usr/local/bin/rustynetd".to_string(),
27744:                     expected_subcommand.to_string(),
27745:                     "--no-fail-on-drift".to_string(),
27746:                 ]
27747:             );
27748:         }
27749:     }

27927:     #[test]
27928:     fn rust_orchestrator_pure_linux_path_delegates_to_bash_orchestrator() {
27929:         // The pure-Linux dispatch path constructs the same bash
27930:         // command shape `LinuxBashOrchestrator` does. We exercise the
27931:         // delegation by inspecting the build_command output of the
27932:         // wrapped orchestrator (the actual bash spawn is not done in
27933:         // this test — that's W3.4 live-lab regression territory).
27934:         let bash = super::LinuxBashOrchestrator::new(PathBuf::from("/usr/local/bin/orch.sh"));
27935:         let inputs = rust_orchestrator_inputs();
27936:         let expected_args = collect_command_args(&bash.build_command(&inputs));
27937:         let rust = super::RustOrchestrator::new(bash, vec![super::VmGuestPlatform::Linux; 5]);
27938:         // Re-construct an equivalent bash orchestrator from the rust
27939:         // wrapper to ensure both paths produce the same argv shape.
27940:         // The wrapper holds the bash orchestrator privately, so we
27941:         // assert via the public route: pure-linux dispatch is
27942:         // identity-by-delegation.
27943:         assert!(rust.is_pure_linux());
27944:         // Sanity: the expected args are the same as the bash impl
27945:         // would emit on its own — the parity contract.
27946:         assert!(
27947:             expected_args.contains(&"--profile".to_string())
27948:                 && expected_args.contains(&"--report-dir".to_string()),
27949:             "bash orchestrator must still build the canonical argv shape: {expected_args:?}"
27950:         );
27951:     }

27964:     fn stage_orchestrator_trait_supports_test_implementations() {
27965:         // Sanity: the trait can be implemented by something that does
27966:         // not spawn bash, so future RustOrchestrator + test fakes can
27967:         // share the dispatch surface without re-implementing the
27968:         // caller's post-processing path.

27977:                     success: true,
27978:                 })
27979:             }
27980:         }
27981:         let inputs = baseline_live_lab_run_inputs();
27982:         let report = StubOrchestrator
27983:             .execute_live_lab(&inputs)
27984:             .expect("stub must return Ok");
27985:         assert!(report.success);

28548:     #[test]
28549:     fn run_linux_daemon_validators_for_aliases_dry_run_prefixes_stage_names_per_alias() {
28550:         let temp = tempfile::TempDir::new().expect("tempdir");
28551:         let report_dir = temp.path().to_path_buf();
28552:         let inventory = temp.path().join("inventory.json");
28553:         std::fs::write(inventory.as_path(), r#"{"version":1,"entries":[]}"#)
28554:             .expect("write inventory");
28555:         let identity = temp.path().join("id_ed25519");
28556:         std::fs::write(identity.as_path(), b"fake-key").expect("write key");
28557:         let aliases = vec!["debian-utm-1".to_string(), "debian-utm-2".to_string()];
28558:         let outcomes = super::run_linux_daemon_validators_for_aliases(
28559:             aliases.as_slice(),
28560:             inventory.as_path(),
28561:             identity.as_path(),
28562:             None,
28563:             report_dir.as_path(),
28564:             true,
28565:         );
28566:         // 6 stages × 2 aliases.
28567:         assert_eq!(outcomes.len(), 12);
28568:         for outcome in &outcomes {
28569:             assert!(
28570:                 outcome.stage.contains("::"),
28571:                 "stage name must be prefixed with alias::: {}",
28572:                 outcome.stage
28573:             );
28574:             assert!(
28575:                 outcome.stage.starts_with("debian-utm-1::")
28576:                     || outcome.stage.starts_with("debian-utm-2::"),
28577:                 "stage prefix must match one of the aliases: {}",
28578:                 outcome.stage
28579:             );
28580:         }
28581:         // Per-alias log subdirs created.
28582:         let validate_root = report_dir.join("validate_linux_daemon_state");
28583:         assert!(validate_root.join("debian-utm-1").is_dir());
28584:         assert!(validate_root.join("debian-utm-2").is_dir());
28585:     }

  15: /// Android adapter — not yet implemented.
  16: /// ADB variant is a lab escape hatch, not a production path.
  17: /// All methods fail closed with a security-specific rejection.
  18: /// See §11 of RustNativeMultiPlatformOrchestratorPlan_2026-04-28.md
  19: /// for what a future W6 track requires before this guard can be lifted.
  20: #[derive(Debug)]
  21: pub struct AndroidNodeAdapter {
  22:     #[allow(dead_code)]
  23:     conn: NodeConnection,
  24:     alias: String,
  25: }
  26: 
  27: impl AndroidNodeAdapter {
  28:     pub fn new(alias: impl Into<String>, conn: NodeConnection) -> Self {
  29:         AndroidNodeAdapter {
  30:             alias: alias.into(),
  31:             conn,
  32:         }
  33:     }
  34: }
  35: 
  36: const ANDROID_UNSUPPORTED_MSG: &str = "\
  37: Android node adapter is not yet implemented. Blocked by security minimum bar: \
  38: (1) no daemon validator coverage — service-hardening-check, key-custody-check, \
  39: dns-failclosed-check not implemented for Android; \
  40: (2) no reviewed key custody model — Android Keystore / StrongBox integration not designed; \
  41: (3) ADB connection model is a lab-only escape hatch — production Android requires \
  42: an app-layer management channel reviewed against security minimum bar.";
  43: 
  44: fn android_unsupported() -> AdapterError {
  45:     AdapterError::UnsupportedPlatform {
  46:         platform: VmGuestPlatform::Android,
  47:         message: ANDROID_UNSUPPORTED_MSG.to_string(),
  48:     }
  49: }
  50: 
  51: impl NodeAdapter for AndroidNodeAdapter {
  52:     fn platform(&self) -> VmGuestPlatform {
  53:         VmGuestPlatform::Android
  54:     }
  55:     fn alias(&self) -> &str {
  56:         &self.alias
  57:     }
  58:     fn install_daemon(
  59:         &self,
  60:         _: &SourceArchive,
  61:         _: &OrchestrationContext,
  62:     ) -> Result<InstallReport, AdapterError> {
  63:         Err(android_unsupported())
  64:     }
  65:     fn start_daemon(&self) -> Result<(), AdapterError> {
  66:         Err(android_unsupported())
  67:     }
  68:     fn stop_daemon(&self) -> Result<(), AdapterError> {
  69:         Err(android_unsupported())
  70:     }
  71:     fn restart_daemon(&self) -> Result<(), AdapterError> {
  72:         Err(android_unsupported())

  10: const IOS_UNSUPPORTED_MSG: &str = "\
  11: iOS node adapter is not yet implemented. Blocked by security minimum bar: \
  12: (1) no daemon validator coverage — service-hardening-check, key-custody-check, \
  13: dns-failclosed-check not implemented for iOS; \
  14: (2) no reviewed key custody model — Secure Enclave / Keychain integration not designed; \
  15: (3) MDM/Network Extension connection model not reviewed against security minimum bar.";
  16: 
  17: const ANDROID_UNSUPPORTED_MSG: &str = "\
  18: Android node adapter is not yet implemented. Blocked by security minimum bar: \
  19: (1) no daemon validator coverage — service-hardening-check, key-custody-check, \
  20: dns-failclosed-check not implemented for Android; \
  21: (2) no reviewed key custody model — Android Keystore / StrongBox integration not designed; \
  22: (3) ADB connection model is a lab-only escape hatch — production Android requires \
  23: an app-layer management channel reviewed against security minimum bar.";
  24: 
  25: /// Build a `NodeAdapter` for the given platform using `conn` as its transport.
  26: /// `alias` must match the `NodeRoleAssignment::alias` for this node.
  27: /// `remote_workdir` is the path to the RustyNet source tree on the remote host;
  28: /// required for Windows `install_daemon`, populated from inventory `rustynet_src_dir`.
  29: ///
  30: /// Error precedence:
  31: /// 1. `ConnectionPlatformMismatch` if connection type is wrong for platform
  32: ///    (e.g. `Adb` + Linux, `Ssh` + iOS).
  33: /// 2. `UnsupportedPlatform` if platform is not yet implemented (iOS, Android)
  34: ///    with a valid connection type — blocked by security minimum bar.
  35: pub fn node_adapter_for(
  36:     alias: impl Into<String>,
  37:     platform: VmGuestPlatform,
  38:     conn: NodeConnection,
  39:     remote_workdir: Option<String>,
  40: ) -> Result<Box<dyn NodeAdapter>, AdapterError> {
  41:     let alias = alias.into();
  42:     // Connection-type check comes first so Ssh+iOS → ConnectionPlatformMismatch,
  43:     // while Mdm+iOS → UnsupportedPlatform.
  44:     if !conn.is_valid_for_platform(&platform) {
  45:         return Err(AdapterError::ConnectionPlatformMismatch {
  46:             platform,
  47:             connection_kind: conn.kind_label(),
  48:         });
  49:     }
  50: 
  51:     match platform {
  52:         VmGuestPlatform::Linux => Ok(Box::new(LinuxNodeAdapter::new(alias, conn))),
  53:         VmGuestPlatform::Windows => Ok(Box::new(WindowsNodeAdapter::new(
  54:             alias,
  55:             conn,
  56:             remote_workdir,
  57:         ))),
  58:         VmGuestPlatform::Macos => Ok(Box::new(MacosNodeAdapter::new(alias, conn, remote_workdir))),
  59:         VmGuestPlatform::Ios => Err(AdapterError::UnsupportedPlatform {
  60:             platform,
  61:             message: IOS_UNSUPPORTED_MSG.to_string(),
  62:         }),
  63:         VmGuestPlatform::Android => Err(AdapterError::UnsupportedPlatform {
  64:             platform,
  65:             message: ANDROID_UNSUPPORTED_MSG.to_string(),
  66:         }),
  67:     }
  68: }
  69:

  22: /// Linux node adapter — full W5.1 implementation.
  23: /// Dispatches all operations via SSH using `NodeConnection::Ssh`.
  24: #[derive(Debug)]

  26:     conn: NodeConnection,

  33:             alias: alias.into(),

 108:     }
 109: 
 110:     // ── Validators ───
 111: 
 112:     fn run_validator(&self, op: DaemonProbeOp) -> Result<ValidatorReport, AdapterError> {
 113:         use crate::vm_lab::{DaemonProbe, LinuxDaemonProbe};
 114:         let probe = LinuxDaemonProbe;
 115:         let argv = probe
 116:             .build_argv(op, linux_install::LINUX_RUSTYNETD_PATH.as_ref())
 117:             .map_err(|message| AdapterError::Protocol { message })?;
 118:         // All argv elements come from `LinuxDaemonProbe::build_argv`, which produces
 119:         // a fixed set of known-safe strings: binary path + a `linux-*-check` subcommand
 120:         // + `--no-fail-on-drift`. No user-controlled input reaches argv.
 121:         let script = argv.join(" ");
 122:         let op_label = argv.get(1).cloned().unwrap_or_default();
 123:         let output = ssh::run_remote(&self.conn, &script, SHORT_TIMEOUT)?;
 124:         let passed = !output.contains("\"passed\": false") && !output.contains("\"passed\":false");
 125:         Ok(ValidatorReport {
 126:             op_label,
 127:             output,
 128:             passed,
 129:         })
 130:     }
 131:

 136:     }
 137: 
 138:     fn probe_denied_peer(&self, denied_ip: &str) -> Result<TrafficTestResult, AdapterError> {

 140:     }
 141:

 143:         linux_traffic::collect_active_tunnels(&self.conn)
 144:     }
 145: 
 146:     // ── Diagnostics + cleanup ───
 147:

 149:         linux_traffic::collect_artifacts(&self.conn, dst)
 150:     }
 151: 
 152:     fn cleanup_runtime_state(&self) -> Result<(), AdapterError> {
 153:         linux_traffic::cleanup_runtime_state(&self.conn)
 154:     }
 155: 
 156:     fn check_ssh_reachable(&self) -> Result<(), AdapterError> {
 157:         linux_traffic::check_ssh_reachable(&self.conn)
 158:     }
 159: 
 160:     fn endpoint(&self) -> String {
 161:         match &self.conn {
 162:             crate::vm_lab::orchestrator::connection::NodeConnection::Ssh { host, .. } => {
 163:                 format!("{host}:51820")
 164:             }
 165:             _ => "0.0.0.0:51820".to_string(),
 166:         }
 167:     }
 168: 
 169:     fn collect_mesh_ip(&self) -> Result<String, AdapterError> {
 170:         linux_traffic::collect_mesh_ip(&self.conn)
 171:     }

 173:     fn issue_bundles_to_dir(
 174:         &self,
 175:         kind: BundleKind,
 176:         env_content: &str,
 177:         local_out_dir: &std::path::Path,
 178:     ) -> Result<(), AdapterError> {
 179:         linux_traffic::issue_bundles_to_dir(
 180:             &self.conn,
 181:             linux_install::LINUX_RUSTYNET_PATH,
 182:             &kind,
 183:             env_content,

===== /crates/rustynet-cli/src/vm_lab/orchestrator/adapter/linux_install.rs =====

   1: #![allow(dead_code)]
   2: use std::io::Write as IoWrite;
   3: use std::time::Duration;
   4: 
   5: use crate::vm_lab::orchestrator::adapter::ssh;
   6: use crate::vm_lab::orchestrator::connection::NodeConnection;
   7: use crate::vm_lab::orchestrator::context::OrchestrationContext;
   8: use crate::vm_lab::orchestrator::error::{AdapterError, InstallReport};
   9: use crate::vm_lab::orchestrator::role::NodeRole;
  10: use crate::vm_lab::orchestrator::source_archive::SourceArchive;
  11: 
  12: /// Canonical path of `rustynetd` on Linux targets.
  13: pub const LINUX_RUSTYNETD_PATH: &str = "/usr/local/bin/rustynetd";
  14: /// Canonical path of `rustynet` CLI on Linux targets.
  15: pub const LINUX_RUSTYNET_PATH: &str = "/usr/local/bin/rustynet";
  16: /// Canonical systemd service name.
  17: pub const LINUX_SERVICE_NAME: &str = "rustynetd";
  18: /// Daemon UNIX socket path.
  19: pub const LINUX_DAEMON_SOCKET: &str = "/run/rustynet/rustynetd.sock";
  20: 
  21: /// Bootstrap script embedded at compile time from the reviewed copy at
  22: /// `scripts/bootstrap/linux/rn_bootstrap.sh`. The script is the same one
  23: /// the bash orchestrator ships via heredoc; factored here so the Rust
  24: /// adapter can scp + invoke it without shelling out to the bash orchestrator.
  25: static BOOTSTRAP_SCRIPT: &str =
  26:     include_str!("../../../../../../scripts/bootstrap/linux/rn_bootstrap.sh");
  27: 
  28: /// Scp the `SourceArchive`, the bootstrap env, and the bootstrap script to
  29: /// the remote host. Then run the bootstrap script and wait for the daemon
  30: /// socket to appear. Returns an `InstallReport` on success.
  31: pub fn install_daemon(
  32:     conn: &NodeConnection,
  33:     alias: &str,
  34:     source: &SourceArchive,
  35:     ctx: &OrchestrationContext,
  36: ) -> Result<InstallReport, AdapterError> {
  37:     let role = ctx
  38:         .assignments
  39:         .iter()
  40:         .find(|a| a.alias == alias)
  41:         .map(|a| &a.role)
  42:         .cloned()
  43:         .unwrap_or(NodeRole::Client);
  44:     let node_id = ctx
  45:         .node_ids
  46:         .get(alias)
  47:         .cloned()
  48:         .unwrap_or_else(|| format!("{alias}-bootstrap"));
  49: 
  50:     // Write bootstrap script to a temp file.
  51:     let script_tmp = write_temp_file("rn_bootstrap_", ".sh", BOOTSTRAP_SCRIPT.as_bytes())?;
  52: 
  53:     // Write env file.
  54:     let env_content = build_bootstrap_env(&node_id, &role, ctx);
  55:     let env_tmp = write_temp_file("rn_bootstrap_env_", ".env", env_content.as_bytes())?;
  56: 
  57:     let short_timeout = Duration::from_secs(30);
  58:     let build_timeout = Duration::from_secs(900); // cargo build can take a while
  59:     let socket_timeout = Duration::from_secs(300);
  60: 
  61:     // SCP the three artefacts.
  62:     ssh::scp_to(
  63:         conn,
  64:         script_tmp.as_path(),
  65:         "/tmp/rn_bootstrap.sh",
  66:         short_timeout,
  67:     )?;
  68:     ssh::scp_to(
  69:         conn,
  70:         env_tmp.as_path(),
  71:         "/tmp/rn_bootstrap.env",
  72:         short_timeout,
  73:     )?;
  74:     ssh::scp_to(conn, source.path(), "/tmp/rn_source.tar.gz", short_timeout)?;
  75: 
  76:     // Cleanup temp files (best-effort; ignore errors).
  77:     let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&script_tmp);
  78:     let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&env_tmp);
  79: 
  80:     // Run bootstrap.
  81:     ssh::run_remote(
  82:         conn,
  83:         "chmod 700 /tmp/rn_bootstrap.sh && bash /tmp/rn_bootstrap.sh /tmp/rn_bootstrap.env",
  84:         build_timeout,
  85:     )?;
  86:     let _ = socket_timeout; // daemon socket is checked in enforce_baseline_runtime / validate_baseline_runtime, not install.
  87: 
  88:     // Verify binaries are present and the rustynetd group exists.
  89:     // /var/lib/rustynet/keys is `drwx------ root:root` (mode 700) by design
  90:     // so the orchestrator's SSH user cannot stat through it without sudo.
  91:     // Using `sudo -n` keeps the check non-interactive and consistent with
  92:     // the bootstrap script's other privileged steps; passwordless sudo is
  93:     // already a precondition of the bootstrap path.
  94:     let verify_script = format!(
  95:         "test -x {rustynetd} && test -x {rustynet} && \
  96:          sudo -n test -f /var/lib/rustynet/keys/wireguard.pub && \
  97:          getent group rustynetd >/dev/null 2>&1",
  98:         rustynetd = LINUX_RUSTYNETD_PATH,
  99:         rustynet = LINUX_RUSTYNET_PATH,
 100:     );
 101:     ssh::run_remote(conn, &verify_script, short_timeout)?;
 102: 
 103:     Ok(InstallReport {
 104:         daemon_path: LINUX_RUSTYNETD_PATH.into(),
 105:         service_name: LINUX_SERVICE_NAME.to_string(),
 106:     })
 107: }
 108: 
 109: /// Start the rustynetd systemd service.
 110: pub fn start_daemon(conn: &NodeConnection) -> Result<(), AdapterError> {
 111:     run_systemctl(conn, "start")
 112: }
 113: 
 114: /// Stop the rustynetd systemd service.
 115: pub fn stop_daemon(conn: &NodeConnection) -> Result<(), AdapterError> {
 116:     run_systemctl(conn, "stop")
 117: }
 118: 
 119: /// Restart the rustynetd systemd service.
 120: pub fn restart_daemon(conn: &NodeConnection) -> Result<(), AdapterError> {
 121:     run_systemctl(conn, "restart")
 122: }
 123: 
 124: /// Stop the service and remove daemon binaries and configuration.
 125: pub fn uninstall_daemon(conn: &NodeConnection) -> Result<(), AdapterError> {
 126:     let timeout = Duration::from_secs(60);
 127:     // Stop service (best-effort — it may not be running).
 128:     let _ = ssh::run_remote(
 129:         conn,
 130:         "if systemctl is-active rustynetd >/dev/null 2>&1; then systemctl stop rustynetd; fi",
 131:         timeout,
 132:     );
 133:     ssh::run_remote(
 134:         conn,
 135:         &format!(
 136:             "rm -f {rustynetd} {rustynet} /etc/systemd/system/rustynetd.service && systemctl daemon-reload 2>/dev/null || true && rm -rf /etc/rustynet /var/lib/rustynet /run/rustynet",
 137:             rustynetd = LINUX_RUSTYNETD_PATH,
 138:             rustynet = LINUX_RUSTYNET_PATH,
 139:         ),
 140:         timeout,
 141:     )?;
 142:     Ok(())
 143: }

 146: 
 147: fn run_systemctl(conn: &NodeConnection, action: &str) -> Result<(), AdapterError> {
 148:     let timeout = Duration::from_secs(60);
 149:     ssh::run_remote(conn, &format!("systemctl {action} rustynetd"), timeout)?;
 150:     Ok(())
 151: }

 153: fn build_bootstrap_env(node_id: &str, role: &NodeRole, ctx: &OrchestrationContext) -> String {
 154:     // `rustynet ops e2e-bootstrap-host --role` only accepts "admin" or "client".
 155:     // The bash orchestrator maps: exit→admin, everything else→client.
 156:     let role_str = match role {
 157:         NodeRole::Exit => "admin",
 158:         _ => "client",
 159:     };
 160:     let ssh_allow_cidrs = &ctx.ssh_allow_cidrs;
 161:     let network_id = &ctx.network_id;
 162:     format!(
 163:         "ROLE={role_str}\nNODE_ID={node_id}\nNETWORK_ID={network_id}\nSSH_ALLOW_CIDRS={ssh_allow_cidrs}\nSOURCE_ARCHIVE=/tmp/rn_source.tar.gz\n"
 164:     )
 165: }
 166: 
 167: /// Write `content` to a temp file with the given prefix and suffix.
 168: /// Returns the temp file path.
 169: fn write_temp_file(
 170:     prefix: &str,
 171:     suffix: &str,
 172:     content: &[u8],
 173: ) -> Result<std::path::PathBuf, AdapterError> {
 174:     let mut path = std::env::temp_dir();
 175:     path.push(format!("{prefix}{}{suffix}", std::process::id()));
 176:     let mut file = std::fs::File::create(&path).map_err(|err| AdapterError::Io {
 177:         message: format!("create temp file failed: {err}"),
 178:     })?;
 179:     file.write_all(content).map_err(|err| AdapterError::Io {
 180:         message: format!("write temp file failed: {err}"),
 181:     })?;
 182:     Ok(path)
 183: }

===== /crates/rustynet-cli/src/vm_lab/orchestrator/adapter/linux_membership.rs =====

   1: #![allow(dead_code)]
   2: use std::path::Path;
   3: use std::time::Duration;
   4: 
   5: use crate::vm_lab::orchestrator::adapter::ssh;
   6: use crate::vm_lab::orchestrator::connection::NodeConnection;
   7: use crate::vm_lab::orchestrator::error::{
   8:     AdapterError, BundleKind, MembershipOwnerKey, MembershipSnapshot, NodeMembershipPeer,
   9: };
  10: use crate::vm_lab::orchestrator::role::NodeRole;
  11: 
  12: const SHORT_TIMEOUT: Duration = Duration::from_secs(30);
  13: const MEDIUM_TIMEOUT: Duration = Duration::from_secs(120);
  14: 
  15: /// Read the membership owner public key from the exit node.
  16: /// The exit node is the only node that holds the owner signing key;
  17: /// calling this on a non-exit node will return an empty key or error.
  18: pub fn issue_membership_owner_key(
  19:     conn: &NodeConnection,
  20: ) -> Result<MembershipOwnerKey, AdapterError> {
  21:     let pem = ssh::run_remote(
  22:         conn,
  23:         "sudo -n cat /etc/rustynet/membership.owner.key.pub 2>/dev/null || \
  24:          sudo -n cat /var/lib/rustynet/membership.owner.key.pub 2>/dev/null || \
  25:          echo ''",
  26:         SHORT_TIMEOUT,
  27:     )?;
  28:     if pem.is_empty() {
  29:         return Err(AdapterError::Protocol {
  30:             message: "membership owner public key not found on remote; \
  31:                       has membership been initialized?"
  32:                 .to_string(),
  33:         });
  34:     }
  35:     Ok(MembershipOwnerKey {
  36:         public_key_pem: pem,
  37:     })
  38: }
  39: 
  40: /// Initialize the membership snapshot on the exit node and return its bytes.
  41: /// Runs `rustynet ops init-membership` for each non-exit peer that is in
  42: /// `peers`, then reads back the snapshot + log from the remote.
  43: pub fn init_membership_snapshot(
  44:     conn: &NodeConnection,
  45:     _owner_key: &MembershipOwnerKey,
  46:     peers: &[NodeMembershipPeer],
  47: ) -> Result<MembershipSnapshot, AdapterError> {
  48:     // 1. Run ops init-membership on the exit node (idempotent if already done).
  49:     //    Privileged: needs to write into /var/lib/rustynet/ (root:rustynetd).
  50:     ssh::run_remote(
  51:         conn,
  52:         "sudo -n env RUSTYNET_NODE_ROLE=admin rustynet ops init-membership",
  53:         MEDIUM_TIMEOUT,
  54:     )?;
  55: 
  56:     // 2. Add each non-exit peer via e2e-membership-add.
  57:     //    Privileged: writes membership.snapshot, reads owner key.
  58:     for peer in peers {
  59:         if peer.role == NodeRole::Exit {
  60:             continue;
  61:         }
  62:         let node_id_arg = shell_safe_arg(&peer.node_id)?;
  63:         let pubkey_arg = hex_32_safe_arg(&peer.public_key_hex)?;
  64:         ssh::run_remote(
  65:             conn,
  66:             &format!(
  67:                 "owner_approver_id=\"$(sudo -n rustynet ops owner-approver-id 2>/dev/null || echo none)\"; \
  68:                  sudo -n rustynet ops e2e-membership-add --client-node-id '{node_id_arg}' \
  69:                  --client-pubkey-hex '{pubkey_arg}' --owner-approver-id \"$owner_approver_id\""
  70:             ),
  71:             MEDIUM_TIMEOUT,
  72:         )?;
  73:     }
  74: 
  75:     // 3. Read back the snapshot bytes. /var/lib/rustynet/ is mode 700 root-owned.
  76:     let snapshot_b64 = ssh::run_remote(
  77:         conn,
  78:         "sudo -n cat /var/lib/rustynet/membership.snapshot | base64 -w 0",
  79:         SHORT_TIMEOUT,
  80:     )?;
  81:     let data = base64_decode(&snapshot_b64)?;
  82:     Ok(MembershipSnapshot { data })
  83: }
  84: 
  85: /// Distribute a signed bundle to this (non-exit) node.
  86: /// The bundle is scp'd to a temp path, then installed atomically via
  87: /// `install -m 0640 -o root -g rustynetd`.
  88: pub fn distribute_signed_bundle(
  89:     conn: &NodeConnection,
  90:     kind: BundleKind,
  91:     bundle_path: &Path,
  92: ) -> Result<(), AdapterError> {
  93:     let (remote_tmp, install_dst) = remote_bundle_paths(&kind);
  94:     // SCP bundle to temp path.
  95:     ssh::scp_to(conn, bundle_path, &remote_tmp, MEDIUM_TIMEOUT)?;
  96:     // Install atomically with correct permissions.
  97:     let install_dir = install_dst
  98:         .rsplit_once('/')
  99:         .map(|(dir, _)| dir)
 100:         .unwrap_or("/var/lib/rustynet");
 101:     // install with -o root and into root-owned directories needs sudo;
 102:     // the bash orchestrator path also runs these via run_root.
 103:     ssh::run_remote(
 104:         conn,
 105:         &format!(
 106:             "sudo -n install -d -m 0700 -o rustynetd -g rustynetd {install_dir} && \
 107:              sudo -n install -m 0640 -o root -g rustynetd '{remote_tmp}' '{install_dst}' && \
 108:              sudo -n rm -f '{remote_tmp}'"
 109:         ),
 110:         SHORT_TIMEOUT,
 111:     )?;
 112:     Ok(())
 113: }
 114: 
 115: // ── Helpers ───
 116: 
 117: fn remote_bundle_paths(kind: &BundleKind) -> (String, String) {
 118:     match kind {
 119:         BundleKind::Membership => (
 120:             "/tmp/rn-membership.snapshot".to_string(),
 121:             "/var/lib/rustynet/membership.snapshot".to_string(),
 122:         ),
 123:         BundleKind::Assignment => (
 124:             "/tmp/rn-assignment.bundle".to_string(),
 125:             "/var/lib/rustynet/rustynetd.assignment".to_string(),
 126:         ),
 127:         BundleKind::Traversal => (
 128:             "/tmp/rn-traversal.bundle".to_string(),
 129:             "/var/lib/rustynet/rustynetd.traversal".to_string(),
 130:         ),
 131:         BundleKind::DnsZone => (
 132:             "/tmp/rn-dns-zone.bundle".to_string(),
 133:             "/var/lib/rustynet/rustynetd.dns-zone".to_string(),
 134:         ),
 135:     }
 136: }
 137: 
 138: /// Reject shell-dangerous characters to prevent injection via alias strings.
 139: fn shell_safe_arg(value: &str) -> Result<String, AdapterError> {
 140:     if value
 141:         .chars()
 142:         .all(|c| c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || matches!(c, '-' | '_' | '.'))
 143:     {
 144:         Ok(value.to_string())
 145:     } else {
 146:         Err(AdapterError::Protocol {
 147:             message: format!(
 148:                 "value '{value}' contains characters not safe for shell argument embedding \
 149:                  (allowed: alphanumeric, hyphen, underscore, dot)"
 150:             ),
 151:         })
 152:     }
 153: }
 154: 
 155: fn hex_32_safe_arg(value: &str) -> Result<String, AdapterError> {
 156:     if NodeMembershipPeer::is_valid_public_key_hex(value) {
 157:         Ok(value.to_string())
 158:     } else {
 159:         Err(AdapterError::Protocol {
 160:             message: "WireGuard public key must be 64 hex chars".to_string(),
 161:         })
 162:     }
 163: }
 164: 
 165: fn base64_decode(encoded: &str) -> Result<Vec<u8>, AdapterError> {
 166:     // Simple base64 decode without pulling in a new crate: delegate to the
 167:     // `base64` crate already used by mod.rs via the `base64` dependency.
 168:     // We access it via `std` since `base64` is workspace-level.
 169:     // For now: spawn `base64 -d` locally on the received bytes.
 170:     // This is an internal implementation detail — the bytes are used only
 171:     // for forwarding the snapshot to non-exit peers, not for cryptographic ops.
 172:     let decoded = base64_std_decode(encoded).map_err(|err| AdapterError::Protocol {
 173:         message: format!("base64 decode of membership snapshot failed: {err}"),
 174:     })?;
 175:     Ok(decoded)
 176: }
 177: 
 178: fn base64_std_decode(encoded: &str) -> Result<Vec<u8>, String> {
 179:     // base64 alphabet: A-Z a-z 0-9 + / = (padding) and whitespace (ignored).
 180:     let clean: String = encoded
 181:         .chars()
 182:         .filter(|c| !c.is_ascii_whitespace())
 183:         .collect();
 184:     // Use base64 via a process call so we don't need direct crate access here.
 185:     // (The base64 crate is available but accessed via the workspace; routing
 186:     // through a shell call is simpler at this layer.)
 187:     use std::process::Command;
 188:     let output = Command::new("base64")
 189:         .arg("-d")
 190:         .stdin(std::process::Stdio::piped())
 191:         .stdout(std::process::Stdio::piped())
 192:         .stderr(std::process::Stdio::piped())
 193:         .spawn()
 194:         .and_then(|mut child| {
 195:             use std::io::Write;
 196:             if let Some(stdin) = child.stdin.take() {
 197:                 let mut stdin = stdin;
 198:                 let _ = stdin.write_all(clean.as_bytes());
 199:             }
 200:             child.wait_with_output()
 201:         })
 202:         .map_err(|err| format!("base64 -d spawn failed: {err}"))?;
 203:     if !output.status.success() {
 204:         let stderr = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr).trim().to_string();
 205:         return Err(format!("base64 -d failed: {stderr}"));
 206:     }
 207:     Ok(output.stdout)
 208: }
 209:

  45: /// Positive connectivity: ping `peer_mesh_ip` 3 times via the tunnel.
  46: /// Returns `TrafficTestResult::Reachable` on success.
  47: pub fn ping_mesh_peer(
  48:     conn: &NodeConnection,
  49:     peer_mesh_ip: &str,
  50: ) -> Result<TrafficTestResult, AdapterError> {
  51:     validate_ip_arg(peer_mesh_ip)?;
  52:     let script = format!("ping -c 3 -W 5 {peer_mesh_ip} >/dev/null 2>&1");
  53:     match ssh::run_remote_check(conn, &script, Duration::from_secs(30))? {
  54:         true => Ok(TrafficTestResult::Reachable),
  55:         false => Ok(TrafficTestResult::Error(format!(
  56:             "ping to {peer_mesh_ip} failed"
  57:         ))),
  58:     }

  61: /// Negative ACL test: confirm `denied_ip` is blocked by default-deny policy.
  62: /// MUST return `TrafficTestResult::Blocked` for the stage to pass.
  63: pub fn probe_denied_peer(
  64:     conn: &NodeConnection,
  65:     denied_ip: &str,
  66: ) -> Result<TrafficTestResult, AdapterError> {
  67:     validate_ip_arg(denied_ip)?;
  68:     // ping with a very short deadline — we expect it to fail immediately.
  69:     let script = format!("ping -c 1 -W 2 {denied_ip} >/dev/null 2>&1");
  70:     match ssh::run_remote_check(conn, &script, Duration::from_secs(10))? {
  71:         // Ping succeeded → traffic reached the denied target → security failure.
  72:         true => Ok(TrafficTestResult::Reachable),
  73:         // Ping failed → as expected, traffic is blocked.
  74:         false => Ok(TrafficTestResult::Blocked),
  75:     }
  76: }

  78: /// Collect list of active WireGuard tunnels from `wg show all latest-handshakes`.
  79: pub fn collect_active_tunnels(conn: &NodeConnection) -> Result<TunnelsList, AdapterError> {
  80:     let output = ssh::run_remote(
  81:         conn,
  82:         "if command -v wg >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
  83:              if sudo -n true >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
  84:                  sudo -n wg show all latest-handshakes 2>&1; \
  85:              else \
  86:                  wg show all latest-handshakes 2>&1; \
  87:              fi; \
  88:          else \
  89:              echo wg-not-installed; \
  90:          fi",
  91:         SHORT_TIMEOUT,
  92:     )?;
  93:     let tunnels: Vec<String> = output
  94:         .lines()
  95:         .filter(|line| !line.is_empty())
  96:         .map(|s| s.to_string())
  97:         .collect();

 101: /// Collect diagnostic artifacts from the remote host to `dst`.
 102: /// Key material paths (`*/keys/*`, `*.priv`, `*.pem`) MUST NOT appear in
 103: /// the archive. This is enforced by the `--exclude` arguments to tar and
 104: /// verified by the key-exclusion invariant test.
 105: pub fn collect_artifacts(conn: &NodeConnection, dst: &std::path::Path) -> Result<(), AdapterError> {
 106:     use std::time::Duration;
 107: 
 108:     let remote_tmp = "/tmp/rn_diag_artifacts.tar.gz";
 109:     // Create archive on remote, excluding key material. /var/lib/rustynet/
 110:     // and /run/rustynet/ are root-owned, mode 700/770; tar needs sudo to
 111:     // read into them. We then chown the archive back so scp_from (running
 112:     // as the SSH user) can read it.
 113:     let tar_script = format!(
 114:         "sudo -n tar -czf {remote_tmp} \
 115:          --exclude='*/keys/*' \
 116:          --exclude='*.priv' \
 117:          --exclude='*.pem' \
 118:          --exclude='*.key' \
 119:          --ignore-failed-read \
 120:          /var/lib/rustynet/ \
 121:          /var/log/ \
 122:          /run/rustynet/ \
 123:          2>/dev/null; \
 124:          sudo -n chown \"$(id -u):$(id -g)\" {remote_tmp} 2>/dev/null; \
 125:          true"
 126:     );
 127:     ssh::run_remote(conn, &tar_script, Duration::from_secs(60))?;
 128: 
 129:     // Download the archive.
 130:     ssh::scp_from(conn, remote_tmp, dst, Duration::from_secs(120))?;
 131: 
 132:     // Remove temp archive from remote (best-effort).
 133:     let _ = ssh::run_remote(conn, &format!("rm -f {remote_tmp}"), SHORT_TIMEOUT);
 134: 
 135:     // Verify the archive contains no key material — security invariant check.
 136:     verify_no_key_material(dst)?;
 137: 
 138:     Ok(())
 139: }

 198: /// Issue signed bundles on this exit node and SCP the results to `local_out_dir`.
 199: pub fn issue_bundles_to_dir(
 200:     conn: &NodeConnection,
 201:     rustynet_path: &str,
 202:     kind: &crate::vm_lab::orchestrator::error::BundleKind,
 203:     env_content: &str,
 204:     local_out_dir: &std::path::Path,
 205: ) -> Result<(), AdapterError> {
 206:     use std::io::Write as IoWrite;
 207:     let pid = std::process::id();
 208:     let remote_env = format!("/tmp/rn_issue_env_{pid}.env");
 209:     let remote_issue_dir = format!("/tmp/rn_issue_{pid}");
 210: 
 211:     let issue_subcmd = match kind {
 212:         crate::vm_lab::orchestrator::error::BundleKind::Assignment => {
 213:             "e2e-issue-assignment-bundles-from-env"
 214:         }
 215:         crate::vm_lab::orchestrator::error::BundleKind::Traversal => {
 216:             "e2e-issue-traversal-bundles-from-env"
 217:         }
 218:         crate::vm_lab::orchestrator::error::BundleKind::DnsZone => {
 219:             "e2e-issue-dns-zone-bundles-from-env"
 220:         }
 221:         crate::vm_lab::orchestrator::error::BundleKind::Membership => {
 222:             return Err(AdapterError::Protocol {
 223:                 message: "Membership bundles are issued via init_membership_snapshot".to_string(),
 224:             });
 225:         }
 226:     };
 227: 
 228:     let mut env_tmp = std::env::temp_dir();
 229:     env_tmp.push(format!("rn_issue_env_{pid}.env"));
 230:     {
 231:         let mut f = std::fs::File::create(&env_tmp).map_err(|e| AdapterError::Io {
 232:             message: format!("create env tmp: {e}"),
 233:         })?;
 234:         f.write_all(env_content.as_bytes())
 235:             .map_err(|e| AdapterError::Io {
 236:                 message: format!("write env tmp: {e}"),
 237:             })?;
 238:     }
 239:     ssh::scp_to(conn, &env_tmp, &remote_env, MEDIUM_TIMEOUT)?;
 240:     let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&env_tmp);
 241: 
 242:     ssh::run_remote(
 243:         conn,
 244:         &format!("mkdir -p '{remote_issue_dir}'"),
 245:         SHORT_TIMEOUT,
 246:     )?;
 247: 
 248:     let safe_rustynet = rustynet_path.replace('\'', "'\"'\"'");
 249:     ssh::run_remote(
 250:         conn,
 251:         &format!(
 252:             "env RUSTYNET_NODE_ROLE=admin sudo -n \
 253:              '{safe_rustynet}' ops {issue_subcmd} \
 254:              --env-file '{remote_env}' --issue-dir '{remote_issue_dir}'"
 255:         ),
 256:         MEDIUM_TIMEOUT,
 257:     )?;
 258: 
 259:     let listing = ssh::run_remote(
 260:         conn,
 261:         &format!("ls -1 '{remote_issue_dir}' 2>/dev/null"),
 262:         SHORT_TIMEOUT,
 263:     )?;
 264: 
 265:     std::fs::create_dir_all(local_out_dir).map_err(|e| AdapterError::Io {
 266:         message: format!("create local out dir: {e}"),
 267:     })?;
 268: 
 269:     for filename in listing.lines().map(str::trim).filter(|s| !s.is_empty()) {
 270:         let remote_path = format!("{remote_issue_dir}/{filename}");
 271:         let local_path = local_out_dir.join(filename);
 272:         ssh::scp_from(conn, &remote_path, &local_path, MEDIUM_TIMEOUT)?;
 273:     }
 274: 
 275:     let _ = ssh::run_remote(
 276:         conn,
 277:         &format!("rm -f '{remote_env}' && rm -rf '{remote_issue_dir}'"),
 278:         SHORT_TIMEOUT,
 279:     );
 280: 
 281:     Ok(())
 282: }

 286: /// Validate that an IP address argument contains no shell-dangerous characters.
 287: fn validate_ip_arg(ip: &str) -> Result<(), AdapterError> {
 288:     if ip
 289:         .chars()
 290:         .all(|c| c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || matches!(c, '.' | ':' | '/'))
 291:     {
 292:         Ok(())
 293:     } else {
 294:         Err(AdapterError::Protocol {
 295:             message: format!(
 296:                 "IP argument '{ip}' contains characters not safe for shell embedding \
 297:                  (allowed: alphanumeric, '.', ':', '/')"
 298:             ),
 299:         })
 300:     }
 301: }

 303: fn decode_wireguard_pubkey_to_hex(value: &str) -> Result<String, String> {
 304:     let decoded = base64_decode_simple(value.as_bytes())
 305:         .map_err(|err| format!("base64 decode of WireGuard public key failed: {err}"))?;
 306:     if decoded.len() != 32 {
 307:         return Err(format!(
 308:             "expected 32-byte WireGuard public key, got {} bytes",
 309:             decoded.len()
 310:         ));
 311:     }
 312:     let mut out = String::with_capacity(64);
 313:     for byte in decoded {
 314:         out.push_str(&format!("{byte:02x}"));
 315:     }
 316:     Ok(out)
 317: }
 318: 
 319: /// Minimal base64 decode that handles the standard alphabet (A-Z, a-z, 0-9, +, /).
 320: /// Used for the 44-char WireGuard key (32 bytes → 44 base64 chars with `=` padding).
 321: fn base64_decode_simple(encoded: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<u8>, String> {
 322:     // Filter out whitespace.
 323:     let filtered: Vec<u8> = encoded
 324:         .iter()
 325:         .copied()
 326:         .filter(|b| !b.is_ascii_whitespace())
 327:         .collect();
 328:     if filtered.is_empty() {
 329:         return Err("empty base64 input".to_string());
 330:     }
 331:     // Lookup table: ASCII byte → 6-bit value (64 = padding, 255 = invalid).
 332:     let mut table = [255u8; 256];
 333:     for (i, ch) in b"ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789+/"
 334:         .iter()
 335:         .enumerate()
 336:     {
 337:         table[*ch as usize] = i as u8;
 338:     }
 339:     table[b'=' as usize] = 64;
 340: 
 341:     let mut output = Vec::with_capacity((filtered.len() * 3) / 4);
 342:     let mut i = 0;
 343:     while i + 3 < filtered.len() {
 344:         let a = table[filtered[i] as usize];
 345:         let b = table[filtered[i + 1] as usize];
 346:         let c = table[filtered[i + 2] as usize];
 347:         let d = table[filtered[i + 3] as usize];
 348:         if a == 255 || b == 255 {
 349:             return Err(format!("invalid base64 character at position {i}"));
 350:         }
 351:         output.push((a << 2) | (b >> 4));
 352:         if c != 64 {
 353:             output.push(((b & 0xf) << 4) | (c >> 2));
 354:         }
 355:         if d != 64 {
 356:             output.push(((c & 0x3) << 6) | d);
 357:         }
 358:         i += 4;
 359:     }
 360:     Ok(output)
 361: }

 363: /// Assert that the collected artifact archive at `path` contains no key material.
 364: /// This is a security invariant: `collect_artifacts` MUST NOT include
 365: /// any file whose path contains `keys/`, ends with `.priv`, or ends with `.pem`.
 366: fn verify_no_key_material(path: &std::path::Path) -> Result<(), AdapterError> {
 367:     use std::process::Command;
 368:     let output = Command::new("tar")
 369:         .arg("-tzf")
 370:         .arg(path.as_os_str())
 371:         .output()
 372:         .map_err(|err| AdapterError::Io {
 373:             message: format!("tar -tzf failed: {err}"),
 374:         })?;
 375:     if !output.status.success() {
 376:         return Err(AdapterError::Io {
 377:             message: "tar -tzf on collected artifact archive returned non-zero".to_string(),
 378:         });
 379:     }
 380:     let listing = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout);
 381:     for entry in listing.lines() {
 382:         if entry.contains("keys/")
 383:             || entry.ends_with(".priv")
 384:             || entry.ends_with(".pem")
 385:             || entry.ends_with(".key")
 386:         {
 387:             return Err(AdapterError::KeyExclusionViolation {
 388:                 path: entry.to_string(),
 389:             });
 390:         }
 391:     }
 392:     Ok(())
 393: }

  29:     /// of transferring a source archive.
  30:     workdir: Option<String>,
  31: }

 120:     fn run_validator(&self, op: DaemonProbeOp) -> Result<ValidatorReport, AdapterError> {
 121:         use crate::vm_lab::{DaemonProbe, MacosDaemonProbe};
 122:         let probe = MacosDaemonProbe;
 123:         let argv = probe
 124:             .build_argv(op, MACOS_RUSTYNETD_PATH.as_ref())
 125:             .map_err(|message| AdapterError::Protocol { message })?;
 126:         let op_label = argv.get(1).cloned().unwrap_or_default();
 127:         // All argv elements come from `MacosDaemonProbe::build_argv`, which produces
 128:         // a fixed set of known-safe strings. No user-controlled input reaches argv.
 129:         let script = argv.join(" ");
 130:         let output = ssh::run_remote(&self.conn, &script, VALIDATOR_TIMEOUT)?;
 131:         let passed = !output.contains("\"passed\": false") && !output.contains("\"passed\":false");
 132:         Ok(ValidatorReport {
 133:             op_label,
 134:             output,
 135:             passed,
 136:         })
 137:     }

  19: pub const MACOS_MEMBERSHIP_OWNER_PUBKEY_PATH: &str =

  25:     include_str!("../../../../../../scripts/bootstrap/macos/Bootstrap-RustyNetMacos.sh");
  26: static INSTALL_SERVICE_SCRIPT: &str =
  27:     include_str!("../../../../../../scripts/bootstrap/macos/Install-RustyNetMacosService.sh");

  29: const SHORT_TIMEOUT: Duration = Duration::from_secs(30);
  30: const BUILD_TIMEOUT: Duration = Duration::from_secs(1800);
  31: const SOCKET_TIMEOUT: Duration = Duration::from_secs(300);
  32: 
  33: /// Bootstrap the daemon on a macOS host. Transfers the source archive and
  34: /// bootstrap script, runs the bootstrap, waits for the daemon socket.
  35: pub fn install_daemon(
  36:     conn: &NodeConnection,
  37:     alias: &str,
  38:     source: &SourceArchive,
  39:     ctx: &OrchestrationContext,
  40: ) -> Result<InstallReport, AdapterError> {
  41:     let role = ctx
  42:         .assignments
  43:         .iter()
  44:         .find(|a| a.alias == alias)
  45:         .map(|a| &a.role)
  46:         .cloned()
  47:         .unwrap_or(NodeRole::Client);
  48:     let node_id = ctx
  49:         .node_ids
  50:         .get(alias)
  51:         .cloned()
  52:         .unwrap_or_else(|| format!("{alias}-bootstrap"));
  53: 
  54:     let script_tmp = write_temp_file("rn_macos_bootstrap_", ".sh", BOOTSTRAP_SCRIPT.as_bytes())?;
  55:     let install_tmp = write_temp_file(
  56:         "rn_macos_install_svc_",
  57:         ".sh",
  58:         INSTALL_SERVICE_SCRIPT.as_bytes(),
  59:     )?;
  60:     let env_content = build_bootstrap_env(&node_id, &role, ctx);
  61:     let env_tmp = write_temp_file("rn_macos_env_", ".env", env_content.as_bytes())?;
  62: 
  63:     ssh::scp_to(
  64:         conn,
  65:         script_tmp.as_path(),
  66:         "/tmp/rn_macos_bootstrap.sh",
  67:         SHORT_TIMEOUT,
  68:     )?;
  69:     ssh::scp_to(
  70:         conn,
  71:         install_tmp.as_path(),
  72:         "/tmp/rn_macos_install_svc.sh",
  73:         SHORT_TIMEOUT,
  74:     )?;
  75:     ssh::scp_to(
  76:         conn,
  77:         env_tmp.as_path(),
  78:         "/tmp/rn_macos_bootstrap.env",
  79:         SHORT_TIMEOUT,
  80:     )?;
  81:     ssh::scp_to(conn, source.path(), "/tmp/rn_source.tar.gz", SHORT_TIMEOUT)?;
  82: 
  83:     let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&script_tmp);
  84:     let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&install_tmp);
  85:     let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&env_tmp);
  86: 
  87:     ssh::run_remote(
  88:         conn,
  89:         "chmod 700 /tmp/rn_macos_bootstrap.sh /tmp/rn_macos_install_svc.sh && \
  90:          sudo bash /tmp/rn_macos_bootstrap.sh /tmp/rn_macos_bootstrap.env",
  91:         BUILD_TIMEOUT,
  92:     )?;
  93: 
  94:     // Daemon socket is checked in enforce_baseline_runtime / validate_baseline_runtime,
  95:     // not at install time — install_daemon only stages binaries + bootstrap state.
  96: 
  97:     let verify_script = format!(
  98:         "test -x {rustynetd} && test -x {rustynet} && \
  99:          test -f {MACOS_KEYS_DIR}/wireguard.pub",
 100:         rustynetd = MACOS_RUSTYNETD_PATH,
 101:         rustynet = MACOS_RUSTYNET_PATH,
 102:     );
 103:     ssh::run_remote(conn, &verify_script, SHORT_TIMEOUT)?;
 104: 
 105:     Ok(InstallReport {
 106:         daemon_path: MACOS_RUSTYNETD_PATH.into(),
 107:         service_name: MACOS_SERVICE_LABEL.to_string(),
 108:     })
 109: }

 111: /// Bootstrap via an existing remote workdir (source already on host).
 112: /// Used when `rustynet_src_dir` is set in inventory.
 113: pub fn install_daemon_from_workdir(
 114:     conn: &NodeConnection,
 115:     alias: &str,
 116:     workdir: &str,
 117:     ctx: &OrchestrationContext,
 118: ) -> Result<InstallReport, AdapterError> {
 119:     if workdir.is_empty() {
 120:         return Err(AdapterError::Protocol {
 121:             message: "install_daemon_from_workdir: workdir must not be empty".to_string(),
 122:         });
 123:     }
 124:     let role = ctx
 125:         .assignments
 126:         .iter()
 127:         .find(|a| a.alias == alias)
 128:         .map(|a| &a.role)
 129:         .cloned()
 130:         .unwrap_or(NodeRole::Client);
 131:     let node_id = ctx
 132:         .node_ids
 133:         .get(alias)
 134:         .cloned()
 135:         .unwrap_or_else(|| format!("{alias}-bootstrap"));
 136: 
 137:     let env_content = build_bootstrap_env(&node_id, &role, ctx);
 138:     let env_tmp = write_temp_file("rn_macos_env_", ".env", env_content.as_bytes())?;
 139:     let script_tmp = write_temp_file("rn_macos_bootstrap_", ".sh", BOOTSTRAP_SCRIPT.as_bytes())?;
 140:     let install_tmp = write_temp_file(
 141:         "rn_macos_install_svc_",
 142:         ".sh",
 143:         INSTALL_SERVICE_SCRIPT.as_bytes(),
 144:     )?;
 145: 
 146:     ssh::scp_to(
 147:         conn,
 148:         env_tmp.as_path(),
 149:         "/tmp/rn_macos_bootstrap.env",
 150:         SHORT_TIMEOUT,
 151:     )?;
 152:     ssh::scp_to(
 153:         conn,
 154:         script_tmp.as_path(),
 155:         "/tmp/rn_macos_bootstrap.sh",
 156:         SHORT_TIMEOUT,
 157:     )?;
 158:     ssh::scp_to(
 159:         conn,
 160:         install_tmp.as_path(),
 161:         "/tmp/rn_macos_install_svc.sh",
 162:         SHORT_TIMEOUT,
 163:     )?;
 164: 
 165:     let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&env_tmp);
 166:     let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&script_tmp);
 167:     let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&install_tmp);
 168: 
 169:     // Inject SOURCE_ARCHIVE pointing to existing workdir archive or skip archive step.
 170:     // Override SOURCE_ARCHIVE to point to a tar of the existing workdir.
 171:     let build_cmd = format!(
 172:         "chmod 700 /tmp/rn_macos_bootstrap.sh /tmp/rn_macos_install_svc.sh && \
 173:          cd '{workdir}' && tar -czf /tmp/rn_source.tar.gz . && \
 174:          echo 'SOURCE_ARCHIVE=/tmp/rn_source.tar.gz' >> /tmp/rn_macos_bootstrap.env && \
 175:          sudo bash /tmp/rn_macos_bootstrap.sh /tmp/rn_macos_bootstrap.env"
 176:     );
 177:     ssh::run_remote(conn, &build_cmd, BUILD_TIMEOUT)?;
 178:     // Daemon socket is checked in enforce_baseline_runtime / validate_baseline_runtime,
 179:     // not at install time — install_daemon only stages binaries + bootstrap state.
 180: 
 181:     Ok(InstallReport {
 182:         daemon_path: MACOS_RUSTYNETD_PATH.into(),
 183:         service_name: MACOS_SERVICE_LABEL.to_string(),
 184:     })
 185: }
 186: 
 187: /// Start the launchd service.
 188: pub fn start_daemon(conn: &NodeConnection) -> Result<(), AdapterError> {
 189:     let plist = "/Library/LaunchDaemons/com.rustynet.daemon.plist";
 190:     // `launchctl bootstrap` is idempotent (errors if already loaded, which we ignore).
 191:     ssh::run_remote(
 192:         conn,
 193:         &format!(
 194:             "sudo launchctl bootstrap system '{plist}' 2>/dev/null || \
 195:              sudo launchctl kickstart system/com.rustynet.daemon 2>/dev/null || true"
 196:         ),
 197:         Duration::from_secs(30),
 198:     )?;
 199:     Ok(())
 200: }
 201: 
 202: /// Stop the launchd service.
 203: pub fn stop_daemon(conn: &NodeConnection) -> Result<(), AdapterError> {
 204:     ssh::run_remote(
 205:         conn,
 206:         "sudo launchctl bootout system/com.rustynet.daemon 2>/dev/null || true",
 207:         Duration::from_secs(30),
 208:     )?;
 209:     Ok(())
 210: }
 211: 
 212: /// Restart the launchd service (stop + start; launchd has no native restart).
 213: pub fn restart_daemon(conn: &NodeConnection) -> Result<(), AdapterError> {
 214:     stop_daemon(conn)?;
 215:     start_daemon(conn)
 216: }
 217: 
 218: /// Stop the service and remove daemon binaries and state.
 219: pub fn uninstall_daemon(conn: &NodeConnection) -> Result<(), AdapterError> {
 220:     let timeout = Duration::from_secs(60);
 221:     let _ = stop_daemon(conn);
 222:     ssh::run_remote(
 223:         conn,
 224:         &format!(
 225:             "sudo rm -f {rustynetd} {rustynet} \
 226:              /Library/LaunchDaemons/com.rustynet.daemon.plist && \
 227:              sudo rm -rf {state_root} /usr/local/etc/rustynet /var/run/rustynet",
 228:             rustynetd = MACOS_RUSTYNETD_PATH,
 229:             rustynet = MACOS_RUSTYNET_PATH,
 230:             state_root = MACOS_STATE_ROOT,
 231:         ),
 232:         timeout,
 233:     )?;
 234:     Ok(())
 235: }

 237: // ── Helpers ───
 238: 
 239: fn build_bootstrap_env(node_id: &str, role: &NodeRole, ctx: &OrchestrationContext) -> String {
 240:     let role_str = match role {
 241:         NodeRole::Exit => "exit",
 242:         NodeRole::Client => "client",
 243:         NodeRole::Entry => "entry",
 244:         NodeRole::Aux => "aux",
 245:         NodeRole::Extra => "extra",
 246:         NodeRole::Custom(s) => s.as_str(),
 247:     };
 248:     format!(
 249:         "ROLE={role_str}\nNODE_ID={node_id}\nNETWORK_ID={network_id}\n\
 250:          SSH_ALLOW_CIDRS={cidrs}\n",
 251:         network_id = ctx.network_id,
 252:         cidrs = ctx.ssh_allow_cidrs,
 253:     )
 254: }
 255: 
 256: fn write_temp_file(
 257:     prefix: &str,
 258:     suffix: &str,
 259:     content: &[u8],
 260: ) -> Result<std::path::PathBuf, AdapterError> {
 261:     let mut path = std::env::temp_dir();
 262:     path.push(format!("{prefix}{}{suffix}", std::process::id()));
 263:     let mut file = std::fs::File::create(&path).map_err(|err| AdapterError::Io {
 264:         message: format!("create temp file failed: {err}"),
 265:     })?;
 266:     file.write_all(content).map_err(|err| AdapterError::Io {
 267:         message: format!("write temp file failed: {err}"),
 268:     })?;
 269:     Ok(path)
 270: }

  12:     AdapterError, BundleKind, MembershipOwnerKey, MembershipSnapshot, NodeMembershipPeer,
  13: };
  14: use crate::vm_lab::orchestrator::role::NodeRole;

  16: const SHORT_TIMEOUT: Duration = Duration::from_secs(30);
  17: const MEDIUM_TIMEOUT: Duration = Duration::from_secs(120);
  18: 
  19: const MACOS_STAGING_DIR: &str = "/tmp/rustynet-staging";

  21: /// Read the membership owner public key from a macOS exit node.
  22: /// Reads `MACOS_MEMBERSHIP_OWNER_PUBKEY_PATH` via SSH `cat`.
  23: pub fn issue_membership_owner_key(
  24:     conn: &NodeConnection,
  25: ) -> Result<MembershipOwnerKey, AdapterError> {
  26:     let pem = ssh::run_remote(
  27:         conn,
  28:         &format!(
  29:             "cat '{path}' 2>/dev/null || echo ''",
  30:             path = MACOS_MEMBERSHIP_OWNER_PUBKEY_PATH
  31:         ),
  32:         SHORT_TIMEOUT,
  33:     )?;
  34:     let pem = pem.trim().to_string();
  35:     if pem.is_empty() {
  36:         return Err(AdapterError::Protocol {
  37:             message: "membership owner public key not found on remote; \
  38:                       has membership been initialized?"
  39:                 .to_string(),
  40:         });
  41:     }
  42:     Ok(MembershipOwnerKey {
  43:         public_key_pem: pem,
  44:     })
  45: }

  47: /// Initialize the membership snapshot on a macOS exit node.
  48: ///
  49: /// Runs `rustynet ops init-membership`, then adds each non-exit peer
  50: /// via `ops e2e-membership-add`, then reads back the snapshot bytes.
  51: /// Requires the SSH session to have sudo / admin privilege.
  52: pub fn init_membership_snapshot(
  53:     conn: &NodeConnection,
  54:     _owner_key: &MembershipOwnerKey,
  55:     peers: &[NodeMembershipPeer],
  56: ) -> Result<MembershipSnapshot, AdapterError> {
  57:     // 1. Run ops init-membership (idempotent).
  58:     ssh::run_remote(
  59:         conn,
  60:         &format!(
  61:             "env RUSTYNET_NODE_ROLE=admin sudo '{rustynet}' ops init-membership",
  62:             rustynet = MACOS_RUSTYNET_PATH,
  63:         ),
  64:         MEDIUM_TIMEOUT,
  65:     )?;
  66: 
  67:     // 2. Add each non-exit peer.
  68:     for peer in peers {
  69:         if peer.role == NodeRole::Exit {
  70:             continue;
  71:         }
  72:         let node_id_arg = shell_safe_arg(&peer.node_id)?;
  73:         let pubkey_arg = hex_32_safe_arg(&peer.public_key_hex)?;
  74:         ssh::run_remote(
  75:             conn,
  76:             &format!(
  77:                 "owner_approver_id=\"$('{rustynet}' ops owner-approver-id 2>/dev/null || echo none)\"; \
  78:                  sudo '{rustynet}' ops e2e-membership-add \
  79:                      --client-node-id '{node_id_arg}' \
  80:                      --client-pubkey-hex '{pubkey_arg}' \
  81:                      --owner-approver-id \"$owner_approver_id\"",
  82:                 rustynet = MACOS_RUSTYNET_PATH,
  83:             ),
  84:             MEDIUM_TIMEOUT,
  85:         )?;
  86:     }
  87: 
  88:     // 3. Read snapshot back as base64.
  89:     let snapshot_b64 = ssh::run_remote(
  90:         conn,
  91:         &format!(
  92:             "cat '{snapshot}' | base64",
  93:             snapshot = MACOS_MEMBERSHIP_SNAPSHOT_PATH,
  94:         ),
  95:         SHORT_TIMEOUT,
  96:     )?;
  97:     let data = base64_decode(snapshot_b64.trim())?;
  98:     Ok(MembershipSnapshot { data })
  99: }
 100: 
 101: /// Distribute a signed bundle to a macOS client node.
 102: /// Uses the same atomic install pattern as Linux: scp to temp, then
 103: /// `sudo install -m 0640 -o root -g rustynetd` to the final path.
 104: pub fn distribute_signed_bundle(
 105:     conn: &NodeConnection,
 106:     kind: BundleKind,
 107:     bundle_path: &Path,
 108: ) -> Result<(), AdapterError> {
 109:     let (remote_tmp, install_dst) = remote_bundle_paths(&kind);
 110:     ssh::scp_to(conn, bundle_path, &remote_tmp, MEDIUM_TIMEOUT)?;
 111:     let install_dir = install_dst
 112:         .rsplit_once('/')
 113:         .map(|(dir, _)| dir)
 114:         .unwrap_or(MACOS_STATE_ROOT);
 115:     ssh::run_remote(
 116:         conn,
 117:         &format!(
 118:             "sudo install -d -m 0700 -o rustynetd -g rustynetd '{install_dir}' && \
 119:              sudo install -m 0640 -o root -g rustynetd '{remote_tmp}' '{install_dst}' && \
 120:              sudo rm -f '{remote_tmp}'"
 121:         ),
 122:         SHORT_TIMEOUT,
 123:     )?;
 124:     Ok(())
 125: }
 126: 
 127: // ── Helpers ───
 128: 
 129: fn remote_bundle_paths(kind: &BundleKind) -> (String, String) {
 130:     let staging = MACOS_STAGING_DIR;
 131:     let state = MACOS_STATE_ROOT;
 132:     match kind {
 133:         BundleKind::Membership => (
 134:             format!("{staging}/rn-membership.snapshot"),
 135:             format!("{state}/membership/membership.snapshot"),
 136:         ),
 137:         BundleKind::Assignment => (
 138:             format!("{staging}/rn-assignment.bundle"),
 139:             format!("{state}/trust/rustynetd.assignment"),
 140:         ),
 141:         BundleKind::Traversal => (
 142:             format!("{staging}/rn-traversal.bundle"),
 143:             format!("{state}/trust/rustynetd.traversal"),
 144:         ),
 145:         BundleKind::DnsZone => (
 146:             format!("{staging}/rn-dns-zone.bundle"),
 147:             format!("{state}/trust/rustynetd.dns-zone"),
 148:         ),
 149:     }
 150: }
 151: 
 152: /// Reject shell-dangerous characters to prevent injection via alias strings.
 153: fn shell_safe_arg(value: &str) -> Result<String, AdapterError> {
 154:     if value
 155:         .chars()
 156:         .all(|c| c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || matches!(c, '-' | '_' | '.'))
 157:     {
 158:         Ok(value.to_string())
 159:     } else {
 160:         Err(AdapterError::Protocol {
 161:             message: format!(
 162:                 "value '{value}' contains characters not safe for shell argument embedding \
 163:                  (allowed: alphanumeric, hyphen, underscore, dot)"
 164:             ),
 165:         })
 166:     }
 167: }
 168: 
 169: fn hex_32_safe_arg(value: &str) -> Result<String, AdapterError> {
 170:     if NodeMembershipPeer::is_valid_public_key_hex(value) {
 171:         Ok(value.to_string())
 172:     } else {
 173:         Err(AdapterError::Protocol {
 174:             message: "WireGuard public key must be 64 hex chars".to_string(),
 175:         })
 176:     }
 177: }
 178: 
 179: fn base64_decode(encoded: &str) -> Result<Vec<u8>, AdapterError> {
 180:     base64_std_decode(encoded).map_err(|err| AdapterError::Protocol {
 181:         message: format!("base64 decode of membership snapshot failed: {err}"),
 182:     })
 183: }
 184: 
 185: fn base64_std_decode(encoded: &str) -> Result<Vec<u8>, String> {
 186:     let clean: String = encoded
 187:         .chars()
 188:         .filter(|c| !c.is_ascii_whitespace())
 189:         .collect();
 190:     use std::io::Write;
 191:     use std::process::{Command, Stdio};
 192:     let output = Command::new("base64")
 193:         .arg("-d")
 194:         .stdin(Stdio::piped())
 195:         .stdout(Stdio::piped())
 196:         .stderr(Stdio::piped())
 197:         .spawn()
 198:         .and_then(|mut child| {
 199:             if let Some(mut stdin) = child.stdin.take() {
 200:                 let _ = stdin.write_all(clean.as_bytes());
 201:             }
 202:             child.wait_with_output()
 203:         })
 204:         .map_err(|err| format!("base64 -d spawn failed: {err}"))?;
 205:     if !output.status.success() {
 206:         let stderr = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr).trim().to_string();
 207:         return Err(format!("base64 -d failed: {stderr}"));
 208:     }
 209:     Ok(output.stdout)
 210: }

  50: /// Ping `peer_mesh_ip` 3 times. Returns `Reachable` on success.
  51: pub fn ping_mesh_peer(
  52:     conn: &NodeConnection,
  53:     peer_mesh_ip: &str,
  54: ) -> Result<TrafficTestResult, AdapterError> {
  55:     validate_ip_arg(peer_mesh_ip)?;
  56:     // macOS `ping` uses -c (count) and -W (wait ms) like Linux.
  57:     let output = ssh::run_remote(
  58:         conn,
  59:         &format!("ping -c 3 -W 1000 '{peer_mesh_ip}' >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo ok || echo fail"),
  60:         Duration::from_secs(30),
  61:     )?;
  62:     if output.trim() == "ok" {
  63:         Ok(TrafficTestResult::Reachable)
  64:     } else {
  65:         Ok(TrafficTestResult::Error(format!(
  66:             "ping to {peer_mesh_ip} failed"
  67:         )))
  68:     }
  69: }

  71: /// Negative ACL test: confirm `denied_ip` is blocked.
  72: pub fn probe_denied_peer(
  73:     conn: &NodeConnection,
  74:     denied_ip: &str,
  75: ) -> Result<TrafficTestResult, AdapterError> {
  76:     validate_ip_arg(denied_ip)?;
  77:     let output = ssh::run_remote(
  78:         conn,
  79:         &format!("ping -c 1 -W 5000 '{denied_ip}' >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo ok || echo fail"),
  80:         Duration::from_secs(15),
  81:     )?;
  82:     if output.trim() == "ok" {
  83:         Ok(TrafficTestResult::Reachable) // reached denied target = security failure
  84:     } else {
  85:         Ok(TrafficTestResult::Blocked) // blocked as expected
  86:     }
  87: }

  89: /// Collect active WireGuard tunnels via `wg show`.
  90: pub fn collect_active_tunnels(conn: &NodeConnection) -> Result<TunnelsList, AdapterError> {

 104: /// Collect diagnostic artifacts from the macOS host to `dst`.
 105: /// Key material paths (`keys/*`, `*.priv`) MUST NOT appear in the archive.
 106: pub fn collect_artifacts(conn: &NodeConnection, dst: &Path) -> Result<(), AdapterError> {
 107:     let remote_tmp = "/tmp/rn_diag_artifacts.tar.gz";
 108: 
 109:     let diag_cmd = format!(
 110:         "tar -czf '{remote_tmp}' \
 111:          --exclude='{MACOS_STATE_ROOT}/keys' \
 112:          --exclude='*.priv' \
 113:          --exclude='*.key' \
 114:          --exclude='*.pem' \
 115:          '{MACOS_STATE_ROOT}' /usr/local/var/log/rustynet 2>/dev/null || \
 116:          tar -czf '{remote_tmp}' --files-from /dev/null"
 117:     );
 118:     ssh::run_remote(conn, &diag_cmd, MEDIUM_TIMEOUT)?;
 119: 
 120:     if let Some(parent) = dst.parent().filter(|p| !p.as_os_str().is_empty()) {
 121:         std::fs::create_dir_all(parent).map_err(|err| AdapterError::Io {
 122:             message: format!("create local artifact destination dir failed: {err}"),
 123:         })?;
 124:     }
 125:     ssh::scp_from(conn, remote_tmp, dst, Duration::from_secs(120))?;
 126: 
 127:     // Remove temp archive from remote (best-effort).
 128:     let _ = ssh::run_remote(conn, &format!("rm -f '{remote_tmp}'"), SHORT_TIMEOUT);
 129: 
 130:     verify_no_key_material_tarball(dst)?;
 131: 
 132:     Ok(())
 133: }

 171: /// Collect the WireGuard mesh IP from the running daemon interface or status.
 172: pub fn collect_mesh_ip(conn: &NodeConnection) -> Result<String, AdapterError> {
 173:     let ip = ssh::run_remote(
 174:         conn,
 175:         "ifconfig 2>/dev/null \
 176:          | grep -A 5 'rustynet\\|utun' \
 177:          | grep 'inet ' \
 178:          | awk '{print $2}' | head -1 || echo ''",
 179:         SHORT_TIMEOUT,
 180:     )?;
 181:     let ip = ip.trim().to_string();
 182:     if !ip.is_empty() {
 183:         return Ok(ip);
 184:     }
 185:     let status = ssh::run_remote(
 186:         conn,
 187:         "RUSTYNET_DAEMON_SOCKET=/var/run/rustynet/rustynetd.sock \
 188:          /usr/local/bin/rustynet status 2>/dev/null || echo ''",
 189:         SHORT_TIMEOUT,
 190:     )?;
 191:     ssh::parse_status_field(&status, "mesh_ip")
 192:         .or_else(|| ssh::parse_status_field(&status, "wg_ip"))
 193:         .ok_or_else(|| AdapterError::Protocol {
 194:             message: "mesh IP not found via ifconfig or rustynet status".to_string(),
 195:         })
 196: }
